=== NOTES 1:207 | Revolutionaries Abroad – India House, Ghadar Party, Berlin Committee, Komagata Maru
## SUB 0 | Ghadar Party (1913) – Founding, Leaders and the 1915 Rising
[207:0:0] # Basic facts
[207:0:1] TABLE head: Particular | Fact
  [207:0:1.0] Founded | 1913, in the USA (North America) by Indian immigrants of the US and Canada; the Hindi Association formed at Portland (Oregon) in May 1913 became the Hindustan Ghadar Party
  [207:0:1.1] Headquarters | Yugantar Ashram, San Francisco (not Berlin, Singapore, Tashkent or Vancouver)
  [207:0:1.2] First president (chairman) | Baba Sohan Singh Bhakna
  [207:0:1.3] General secretary / moving spirit | Lala Har Dayal – the leader and organiser; came to the US in 1911 (lectured at Stanford)
  [207:0:1.4] Treasurer | Pandit Kanshi Ram
  [207:0:1.5] Members | Mainly Punjabi Sikh peasants and ex-soldiers settled on the Pacific coast of North America
  [207:0:1.6] Meaning of "Ghadar" | Revolt / mutiny
  [207:0:1.7] Paper Ghadar | A weekly, for free circulation; first issue 1 November 1913, in Urdu (Gurmukhi edition a month later); masthead "Angrezi Raj ka Dushman"; poems collected as *Ghadar ki Goonj*
[207:0:2] - **Founder:** books credit **Lala Har Dayal** (organiser, secretary) together with **Sohan Singh Bhakna** (founder-president).
[207:0:3] - **Programme:** assassinate officials, publish revolutionary literature, work among Indian troops abroad, procure arms, and bring about a **simultaneous revolt in all British colonies**; ideology strongly **secular**.
[207:0:4] # Leaders – who was and who was not
[207:0:5] - **Ghadarites:** Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, **Ramchandra**, Bhagwan Singh, **Kartar Singh Sarabha** (sub-editor of *Ghadar*), **Barkatullah**, **Bhai Parmanand**, **Rash Behari Bose** (led the 1915 rising).
[207:0:6] - **NOT Ghadarites:** **Surya Sen** (Chittagong, 1930), **Khudiram Bose** (Muzaffarpur bomb, 1908), Barindra Kumar Ghosh, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee.
[207:0:7] - **Pre-Ghadar work in North America:** Ramnath Puri, **G.D. Kumar**, **Taraknath Das**, Sohan Singh Bhakna.
[207:0:8] TABLE head: Body | Place
  [207:0:8.0] Swadesh Sevak Home (G.D. Kumar, 1909) | Vancouver
  [207:0:8.1] United India House (Taraknath Das and G.D. Kumar, 1910) | Seattle
  [207:0:8.2] Yugantar Ashram (Ghadar HQ) | San Francisco
  [207:0:8.3] INA / Azad Hind Fauj (1940s) | Singapore, later Rangoon
[207:0:9] # The rising of 1915
[207:0:10] - **Triggers (1914):** Har Dayal's arrest (March 1914), the **Komagata Maru** incident and, above all, the **outbreak of the First World War** – "England's difficulty, India's opportunity".
[207:0:11] - **21 February 1915:** date fixed for an armed revolt in the **Ferozepur, Lahore and Rawalpindi** garrisons; foiled by **treachery**.
[207:0:12] - **Defence of India Act (March 1915)** passed mainly to crush the Ghadar; **45 hanged** (Spectrum; PMF gives 42).
[207:0:13] - **Lahore Conspiracy Case (1915):** against the Ghadarites – **Kartar Singh Sarabha** and **Vishnu Ganesh Pingle** executed (16 Nov 1915); Bhai Parmanand arrested; Sohan Singh Bhakna transported for life.
[207:0:14] - **Singapore mutiny (15 February 1915):** 5th Light Infantry, inspired by the Ghadar.
[207:0:15] > Trap: Ghadar = **USA / North America, 1913, San Francisco**; first president **Bhakna**, leader and organiser **Har Dayal**; the 1915 rising was set off by the **First World War**.
[207:0:16] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.319-325; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.86-91; NextGen Indian History 06 p.54, p.78; Rocket Indian History Part 2; app notes 1:207 (sub 1, 2)
[207:0:17] - **Sohan Singh Bhakna** called **Kartar Singh Sarabha** his "General".
[207:0:18] - **Origin:** the party grew out of the **Pacific Coast Hindustan Association** (Hindi Association), San Francisco / Portland, 1913.
## SUB 1 | India House, London and Revolutionaries in Europe
[207:1:0] # Shyamji Krishnavarma – London, 1905
[207:1:1] TABLE head: Body | Founder | Place, year
  [207:1:1.0] Indian Home Rule Society | Shyamji Krishnavarma | London, February 1905
  [207:1:1.1] India House (hostel for Indian students) | Shyamji Krishnavarma | London, 1905
  [207:1:1.2] *The Indian Sociologist* (journal) | Shyamji Krishnavarma | London, 1905
  [207:1:1.3] Paris Indian Society | Madame Bhikaji Cama (with S.R. Rana) | Paris, 1905
[207:1:2] - **India House circle:** **Savarkar**, **Har Dayal**, **Madan Lal Dhingra**; Savarkar led it after Krishnavarma left for Paris (1907); it broke up after 1909.
[207:1:3] - Not founders of India House: Rash Behari Bose, Taraknath Das, Barkatullah, Virendranath Chattopadhyay, Har Dayal; Annie Besant, Tilak and Gandhi did **not** start the Indian Home Rule Society (Besant and Tilak had the 1916 Home Rule Leagues).
[207:1:4] # Madan Lal Dhingra (1909)
[207:1:5] - **1 July 1909, London:** shot **Sir William Curzon Wyllie** (political ADC at the India Office) and **Cowasji Lalkaka**.
[207:1:6] - **Hanged at Pentonville Prison, London (1909)** – not life imprisonment.
[207:1:7] - **Hanged for killing British officers in England:** **Madan Lal Dhingra** (1909) and **Udham Singh** (Michael O'Dwyer, 1940).
[207:1:8] # Madame Bhikaji Cama
[207:1:9] - Born to a rich **Parsi** family of Bombay (1861); went to London in 1902; worked as **Dadabhai Naoroji's private secretary**; then based in **Paris** (and Geneva).
[207:1:10] - **22 August 1907:** unfurled the Indian flag at the **International Socialist Congress, Stuttgart (Germany)** – the **first woman** (first person) to hoist an Indian flag abroad; not Paris, London or Geneva.
[207:1:11] - Brought out **Bande Mataram** from Paris; popularly called the "**Mother of the Indian Revolution**".
[207:1:12] - **Prominent revolutionaries abroad:** **Bhikaji Cama, M. Barkatullah, V.V.S. Iyer, M.N. Roy** (UPSC 1994).
[207:1:13] > Statement trap (IAS 2006): Cama's flag = **Stuttgart**, not Paris ✗; Naoroji's private secretary ✓; Parsi ✓ → "II and III".
[207:1:14] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.319-320, p.324-325; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.75-76, p.107; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhikaiji_Cama; app notes 1:207 (sub 0, 4, 6)
## SUB 2 | Komagata Maru (1914)
[207:2:0] TABLE head: Particular | Fact
  [207:2:0.0] What | A Japanese steamship carrying Indian would-be immigrants to Canada (not a party, a Chinese village or a leader)
  [207:2:0.1] Chartered by | Baba Gurdit Singh, a Punjabi contractor based in Singapore (misprinted "Gurdip Singh" in UPPCS 2014)
  [207:2:0.2] Passengers | 376 (mostly Sikhs, also Muslims and Hindus)
  [207:2:0.3] Route | Left Hong Kong (4 April 1914) → Shanghai, Moji, Yokohama → Vancouver (arrived 23 May 1914)
  [207:2:0.4] Why refused | Canada's "continuous journey" rule
  [207:2:0.5] Return | Forced back; reached Budge Budge near Calcutta – police firing on 29 September 1914 (Spectrum: 22 died; PMF: 18)
  [207:2:0.6] Impact | Fury in Punjab; spurred the Ghadar rising
[207:2:1] - **2016:** Canadian PM **Justin Trudeau** apologised in the House of Commons.
[207:2:2] > Sequence: **Komagata Maru (1914) → Gandhi's return (9 January 1915) → Tilak's Home Rule League (April 1916)**.
[207:2:3] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.321; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.89; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komagata_Maru_incident; app notes 1:207 (sub 3)
## SUB 3 | Berlin Committee and the Provisional Government at Kabul (1915)
[207:3:0] - **Berlin Committee for Indian Independence (1915):** **Virendranath Chattopadhyaya**, **Bhupendranath Dutta**, Lala Har Dayal, with the German foreign office ("Zimmerman Plan"); sought help of **Germany and Turkey**.
[207:3:1] - Missions went to **Baghdad, Persia, Turkey and Kabul**.
[207:3:2] TABLE head: Provisional Government of India, Kabul (Afghanistan), 1 December 1915 | Person
  [207:3:2.0] President | Raja Mahendra Pratap
  [207:3:2.1] Prime Minister | Maulana Barkatullah
  [207:3:2.2] Member | Obaidullah Sindhi
[207:3:3] - Set up during the **First World War**, with German and Turkish backing and the help of the Afghan crown prince **Amanullah**; it was a **republican government abroad** – not Bose's (Azad Hind, 1943).
[207:3:4] - **Period:** December 1915 – the wartime phase of the Ghadar and Berlin efforts, just before the Home Rule Leagues (1916); keys put it in the "Home Rule Movement" period.
[207:3:5] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.322-323; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.76-77; NextGen Indian History 06 p.78; app notes 1:207 (sub 5)
[207:3:6] - **Significance:** the revolutionaries abroad **internationalised** the struggle – arms, funds and foreign support (Germany, Turkey, Afghanistan) in the First World War.
## SUB 4 | Newspapers Abroad and M.N. Roy
[207:4:0] TABLE head: Paper | Person | Place
  [207:4:0.0] Indian Sociologist | Shyamji Krishnavarma | London
  [207:4:0.1] Ghadar | Har Dayal (Punjabi edition: Kartar Singh Sarabha) | San Francisco
  [207:4:0.2] Free Hindustan (1908) | Taraknath Das | Vancouver / North America
  [207:4:0.3] Swadesh Sevak (Gurmukhi) | G.D. (Guru Dutt) Kumar – not B.C. Pal | Vancouver
  [207:4:0.4] Talwar | Virendranath Chattopadhyay | Berlin
  [207:4:0.5] Islamic Fraternity | Muhammad Barkatullah | Tokyo
  [207:4:0.6] Bande Mataram (abroad) | Bhikaji Cama | Paris
  [207:4:0.7] Vanguard (1922) | M.N. Roy | Émigré Communist journal
  [207:4:0.8] Comrade | Muhammad Ali | Calcutta / Delhi
  [207:4:0.9] Vande Mataram (Calcutta, 1906) | Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo | Calcutta
[207:4:1] - **M.N. Roy:** founded the **Communist Party of Mexico** and the **CPI at Tashkent (1920)**; paper **Vanguard**; book *India in Transition*; later the **Radical Democratic Party (1940)**.
[207:4:2] > Match (APPSC G1): Indian Sociologist – **Krishnavarma**; Islamic Fraternity – **Barkatullah**; Talwar – **Chattopadhyay**; Swadesh Sevak – **G.D. Kumar**.
[207:4:3] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.320-321; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.87, p.107; NextGen Indian History 06 p.77; NextGen AP History 19 p.13; app notes 1:207 (sub 7, 8)
## SUB 5 | Andhra Link – Darsi Chenchaiah
[207:5:0] - **Darsi (Dasari) Chenchaiah** of **Kanigiri** – the **only Telugu member of the Ghadar Party**; worked for it in America (1912-15); arrested on suspicion; autobiography **Nenu Naa Desam**; later a communist.
[207:5:1] - Distractors: Chandra Rajeswara Rao, Jonnalagadda Ramalingaiah, Siva Varma.
[207:5:2] - **Sohan Singh Bhakna** attended the **Palasa Kisan Sabha (March 1940)**.
[207:5:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History 19 p.13, p.16; NextGen Modern L3 Part 1 p.79, p.105; app notes 1:207 (sub 8)

=== NOTES 1:208 | Home Rule Movement – Tilak and Annie Besant; Impact
## SUB 0 | The Two Home Rule Leagues (1916)
[208:0:0] # Why and when
[208:0:1] - **Home Rule Movement** = the popular movement of India **during the First World War** (not Swadeshi, Separatist or Swaraj Party); on the lines of the **Irish Home Rule Leagues**; aim **self-government within the British Empire**.
[208:0:2] - Causes: need for popular pressure, disillusion with the **Morley-Minto reforms**, wartime miseries; **Tilak released from Mandalay (June 1914)** after six years.
[208:0:3] - **Two leagues, 1916**, led by **Tilak and Annie Besant** (not Aurobindo, Lajpat Rai or B.C. Pal); they demarcated areas and cooperated.
[208:0:4] # Comparison
[208:0:5] TABLE head: Feature | Tilak's Indian Home Rule League | Besant's All India Home Rule League
  [208:0:5.0] Founded | April 1916 (28 April) – the first league | September 1916
  [208:0:5.1] Place | Launched at the Bombay Provincial Conference, Belgaum; headquarters Poona | Madras (HQ Adyar)
  [208:0:5.2] Area | Maharashtra (except Bombay city), Karnataka, Central Provinces, Berar | Rest of India, including Bombay city
  [208:0:5.3] Branches | 6 | about 200
  [208:0:5.4] Office-bearers | President Joseph Baptista; Secretary N.C. Kelkar | Organising secretary George Arundale; C.P. Ramaswamy Aiyar, B.P. Wadia
[208:0:6] - **Associated leaders:** **S. Subramania Iyer** (co-leader with Besant), G.S. Khaparde, Joseph Baptista, **Jinnah** (Bombay; also popularised it in UP), Motilal and Jawaharlal Nehru, Madan Mohan Malaviya, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Lajpat Rai.
[208:0:7] - **H.S. Olcott** – co-founder of the **Theosophical Society** (died 1907), **not** a Home Rule leader.
[208:0:8] - **C.R. Das** – the usual answer for "not associated" (he only joined the agitation later; Spectrum p.329 lists him among those who joined).
[208:0:9] - **1915 Bombay Congress:** Besant **failed** to get the Congress to approve her Home Rule League scheme – no Home Rule resolution.
[208:0:10] # Fate
[208:0:11] - Tilak's League later merged with Besant's; **1920:** Gandhi became President of the **All India Home Rule League** and renamed it **Swarajya Sabha**; it soon merged into the Congress.
[208:0:12] - **Year of merger of the two leagues = 1920** (not 1916, 1918 or 1923).
[208:0:13] > Statement trap (APPSC FRO): "Tilak founded the Indian Home Rule League in **1914** and was its **president**" ✗ (April 1916; president Joseph Baptista); "Tilak played a key role in the **Lucknow Pact (1916)** with Jinnah" ✓.
[208:0:14] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.327-331; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.94-97; NextGen Indian History 06 p.53-54, p.72; app notes 1:208 (sub 0, 1)
[208:0:15] - **Order:** Komagata Maru (1914) → Gandhi's return (Jan 1915) → Tilak's League (Apr 1916) → Besant's (Sep 1916) → Lucknow Pact (Dec 1916) → Montagu Declaration (Aug 1917).
[208:0:16] - **Madras Home Rule League:** General Secretary **C.P. Ramaswamy Aiyar**, Treasurer **B.P. Wadia**.
## SUB 1 | Annie Besant – Theosophist, Papers and Congress President
[208:1:0] # Life and institutions
[208:1:1] - Irish theosophist; came to India in **1893**; President of the **Theosophical Society** from **1907** (HQ Adyar); called the "**Iron Lady of Ireland**".
[208:1:2] - **Central Hindu College, Varanasi (1898)** – became the core of **Banaras Hindu University**, whose founder is **Madan Mohan Malaviya** (1916) – not Besant or Asutosh Mukherjee.
[208:1:3] - **National College, Madanapalle (1916)** – first principal **J.H. Cousins**; protégé **Jiddu Krishnamurti** (*At the Feet of the Master*).
[208:1:4] # Her papers
[208:1:5] TABLE head: Paper | Fact
  [208:1:5.0] The Commonweal | English weekly, Madras, January 1914 – editor Annie Besant
  [208:1:5.1] New India | She bought the *Madras Standard* (July 1914) and renamed it New India (a daily)
[208:1:6] - **Both papers = Besant** (APPSC G2 Mains 2025); "New Hindu" and "The Aryans" are distractors; New India ≠ Gandhi.
[208:1:7] # Congress President and later work
[208:1:8] TABLE head: President | Session | Fact
  [208:1:8.0] Annie Besant | Calcutta, 1917 | First woman President of the INC
  [208:1:8.1] Sarojini Naidu | Kanpur, 1925 | First Indian woman President
  [208:1:8.2] Nellie Sengupta | Calcutta, 1933 | After president-elect Malaviya was arrested
[208:1:9] - Sucheta Kripalani, Aruna Asaf Ali, Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit, Kasturba – never INC presidents.
[208:1:10] - **1918:** Besant visited **Bihar (Patna)** to strengthen the Home Rule League.
[208:1:11] - Quote: "**I am an Indian Tom-Tom**, whose work is waking up all the sleepers…" – **Annie Besant**.
[208:1:12] - **Chief architect** of the **Moderate–Extremist reunion** at Lucknow (1916), with Tilak.
[208:1:13] # Commonwealth of India Bill (1925)
[208:1:14] - Drafted by the **National Convention** (Sapru); amended by an All Parties Conference sub-committee chaired by **Besant**; introduced in the House of Commons by **George Lansbury** (Labour), **December 1925**; defeated.
[208:1:15] - Proposed **dominion status** ("equal footing with the self-governing dominions") and a **parliamentary system**; its Article 7 listed **seven fundamental rights**.
[208:1:16] - Called the "Dominion of India Bill" in the APPSC key – not the Nehru Report (1928) or the Sapru Report.
[208:1:17] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.328-329, p.643; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.96; NextGen Indian History 06 p.68, p.70, p.77; https://constitutionofindia.net/historical-constitution/the-commonwealth-of-india-bill-national-convention-india-1925; app notes 1:208 (sub 3, 4, 5, 6)
## SUB 2 | Tilak, Lucknow 1916 and the Lucknow Pact
[208:2:0] # Tilak
[208:2:1] - **"Father of Indian Unrest"** – **Valentine Chirol** (*Indian Unrest*); Tilak went to England (Sept 1918) to fight a libel case against him.
[208:2:2] - **"Lokmanya"** ("beloved / respected by the people") – exam keys tie it to the **Home Rule Movement**; Spectrum p.593 says he got it after his **1897 sedition trial**.
[208:2:3] - "**Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it**" – Tilak; papers **Kesari (Marathi)** and **Mahratta (English)**.
[208:2:4] - Other quotes of the period: "The British Empire is **rotten to the core**, corrupt in every direction…" – **Sister Nivedita** (not Besant); "First we are Indians, then only Muslims" – **Jinnah**.
[208:2:5] # Lucknow session, December 1916
[208:2:6] - President **A.C. Majumdar**; the **Surat split (1907)** healed – Extremists readmitted; helped by Tilak's and Besant's efforts and the deaths of Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta (1915).
[208:2:7] - The session where the **Home Rule supporters demonstrated their political power** (the Home Rule Leagues held a joint meeting of 1,000+ delegates).
[208:2:8] - **Lucknow Pact (Congress–League):** negotiated by **Tilak and Jinnah**; Congress accepted **separate electorates**; "**Better two united fists…**" – Tilak.
[208:2:9] - Tilak proposed at Lucknow a small **Working Committee** to turn the Congress into a body able to lead a sustained movement (created only in 1920).
[208:2:10] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.331-334, p.593; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.93-97; NextGen Indian History 06 p.54; app notes 1:208 (sub 2, 6, 7); Working Committee proposal and Nivedita quote: general knowledge, not checked
## SUB 3 | Impact, Decline and the August Declaration
[208:3:0] # Repression and the British answer
[208:3:1] - **June 1917:** Besant, **B.P. Wadia** and **George Arundale** interned (Ootacamund); S. Subramania Aiyar renounced his knighthood; released **September 1917**.
[208:3:2] - Montagu: "Shiva … cut his wife into fifty-two pieces …" – on the folly of interning Besant.
[208:3:3] - **Montagu (August) Declaration, 20 August 1917:** by **Edwin Montagu**, Secretary of State (not Morley, Minto or Chelmsford) – "**progressive realisation of responsible government**" through self-governing institutions.
[208:3:4] # Why it faded (1918-19)
[208:3:5] - Moderates pacified by the reform promise; Besant's vacillation; the **Montford reforms (July 1918)** split the ranks; Tilak away in England; Gandhi's rise.
[208:3:6] # Why it was a new phase
[208:3:7] - It put the demand for **self-government (Home Rule)** before the nation as a clear programme; shifted the emphasis from the elite to the **masses**; linked town and country; created a generation of nationalists; prepared the ground for Gandhian politics.
[208:3:8] - It **filled the gap** between **Gokhale's death (1915)** and **Gandhi's rise**.
[208:3:9] - Not because Gandhi led it or because of Hindu-Muslim struggle (that is the Lucknow Pact / Khilafat).
[208:3:10] # Papers of the Home Rule era
[208:3:11] TABLE head: Paper | Person
  [208:3:11.0] Young India | Started (1916-19) as a weekly by the Home Rule party (Jamnadas Dwarkadas, Shankarlal Banker of Besant's league); Gandhi's from Oct 1919
  [208:3:11.1] The Leader | Madan Mohan Malaviya, Allahabad – mouthpiece of the Liberals
  [208:3:11.2] New India / Commonweal | Annie Besant
  [208:3:11.3] Free Press Journal | English daily (1930)
[208:3:12] # World-war context
[208:3:13] - **First World War (1914-18):** the **Treaty of Versailles (1919)** humiliated **Germany**.
[208:3:14] - **Second World War (1939-45):** the **deadliest conflict** in history by total casualties.
[208:3:15] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.330-331, p.335; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.96-98; Rocket Indian History Part 1 (newspapers table); app notes 1:208 (sub 4, 8); world-war facts: general knowledge, not checked
[208:3:16] - **Besant released 17 September 1917**, then elected INC President (Calcutta, December 1917).
[208:3:17] - **Congress special session, Bombay (August 1918)**, under **Hasan Imam**, split over the Mont-Ford proposals.
[208:3:18] - **Effect of the internment:** nationwide protest; it **strengthened** the movement and drew in the Moderates (Jinnah, Surendranath Banerjea, Malaviya).

=== NOTES 1:209 | Revolutionary Nationalism – Second Phase: Hsra, Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, Surya Sen, Kakori and Lahore Cases
## SUB 0 | Lahore Conspiracy Case (1929-31), the Executions and Jatin Das
[209:0:0] # The case
[209:0:1] - **Trial:** Bhagat Singh, **Sukhdev**, **Rajguru** and others were tried for the **Saunders murder** (and bomb-making) in the **Lahore Conspiracy Case** before a **special tribunal set up by the Governor-General**; the **death sentence came in October 1930**.
[209:0:2] - Bhagat Singh had already got life in the **Assembly Bomb Case**; the sentence waited for the verdict in the Saunders (Lahore) case.
[209:0:3] - The accused turned the **court into a forum of propaganda**; the **defence was organised by Congress leaders**.
[209:0:4] - **"Second" Lahore case:** the **first Lahore Conspiracy Case (1915)** was the **Ghadar** case – the first trial under the **Defence of India Act, 1915** (passed mainly to deal with the Ghadarites).
[209:0:5] TABLE head: Sentence | Revolutionaries
  [209:0:5.0] Hanged, 23 March 1931, Lahore jail | Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru
  [209:0:5.1] Transportation for life | Kishori Lal, Mahabir Singh, Bejoy Kumar Sinha, Shiv Verma, Gaya Prasad, Jaidev Kapur, Kamalnath Tewari
  [209:0:5.2] Life (Assembly Bomb Case), not hanged | Batukeshwar Dutt
[209:0:6] > NOT hanged in the Lahore case: **B.K. Dutt** (life), **Bismil, Roshan Singh** (Kakori, 1927), **Azad** (died at Alfred Park, Feb 1931).
[209:0:7] - Cremated at **Hussainiwala**, banks of the **Sutlej**, **Ferozpur district** – today the **Shaheed Bhagat Singh memorial** (B.K. Dutt was also cremated there, 1965).
[209:0:8] # Lahore jail hunger strike (1929)
[209:0:9] - Demand: **honourable treatment as political prisoners**; Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, B.K. Dutt, **Jatin Das** and others fasted.
[209:0:10] - **Jatin (Jatindra Nath) Das** – earlier in **Non-Cooperation (1921)**; made bombs for the HSRA; arrested **14 June 1929** in the (supplementary) **Lahore Conspiracy Case**; **died after 63 days** of fasting (Spectrum: "on the 64th day"), **September 1929** – the freedom fighter who **died in jail on hunger strike**.
[209:0:11] # Cases in order
[209:0:12] TABLE head: Case | Year
  [209:0:12.0] First Lahore (Ghadar) | 1915
  [209:0:12.1] Kanpur (Bolshevik) conspiracy | 1924
  [209:0:12.2] Kakori | 1925
  [209:0:12.3] Meerut (31 communists) | 1929
  [209:0:12.4] Second Lahore (Bhagat Singh) | 1929-31
[209:0:13] ~~ Sources: Spectrum (Ahir) p.383, p.388, p.325; PMF Modern History Part 4 p.164; NextGen Indian History APPSC 06 p.78; old app notes (life sentences, Hussainiwala, Jatin Das arrest date)
## SUB 1 | HRA (1924) and HSRA (1928)
[209:1:0] TABLE head: Feature | HRA – Hindustan Republican Association/Army | HSRA – Hindustan Socialist Republican Association/Army
  [209:1:0.0] Founded | October 1924, Kanpur | 9-10 September 1928, Ferozshah Kotla, Delhi
  [209:1:0.1] Founders / leader | Sachindranath Sanyal, Ram Prasad Bismil, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjee | Reorganised and renamed under Chandra Shekhar Azad
  [209:1:0.2] Members | Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri, Manmathnath Gupta, Azad | Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Bhagwati Charan Vohra (Punjab); Bejoy Kumar Sinha, Shiv Verma, Jaidev Kapur (UP); Rajguru, B.K. Dutt
  [209:1:0.3] Goal | Armed revolution → Federal Republic of the United States of India, adult franchise | Same republic + socialism as the official goal; collective leadership
  [209:1:0.4] Main action | Kakori (1925) | Saunders (1928), Assembly bomb (1929)
[209:1:1] - **Azad** (not Bhagat Singh) **renamed** the HRA as the **HSRA**; Bhagat Singh is credited as a **founder (leader) of the HSRA**, never of the HRA.
[209:1:2] - **HRA founders – dispute:** Spectrum, PMF and Wikipedia name **Sanyal, Bismil, Chatterjee** only; **NextGen and the APPSC G1 2024 key also list Azad**, who joined as a member.
[209:1:3] - **Shiv Verma** came in with the **HSRA** (1928), not the HRA.
[209:1:4] - HSRA-era methods: **mass propaganda** – courtroom statements, leaflets, **hunger strikes**.
[209:1:5] - **AP link:** a "Hindustan Socialist Republican Army" in **Madras (10 March 1933)** – **Kanuru Ramanatha Choudary**.
[209:1:6] TABLE head: Body | Founder / region
  [209:1:6.0] Naujawan Bharat Sabha (Lahore, 1926) | Bhagat Singh
  [209:1:6.1] Indian Republican Army (Chittagong) | Surya Sen
  [209:1:6.2] Abhinav Bharat | V.D. Savarkar
  [209:1:6.3] Anushilan Samiti | Bengal (Aurobindo associated)
  [209:1:6.4] Kuka movement | Guru Ram Singh
  [209:1:6.5] Khudai Khidmatgar | Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan
[209:1:7] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.381-382; PMF Part 4 p.162-163, p.169; NextGen APPSC 06 p.73; en.wikipedia.org Hindustan Socialist Republican Association; old app notes (AP link)
## SUB 2 | Kakori Train Action (9 August 1925)
[209:2:0] - **HRA** men held up the **8-Down train at Kakori near Lucknow** (Lucknow-Saharanpur section) and **looted official railway cash (government treasury)** to **finance the organisation**; one passenger was killed by accident.
[209:2:1] - **43 arrested**; public prosecutor (government advocate): **Jagat Narain Mulla**; defence committee chaired by **Govind Ballabh Pant** (with Chandra Bhanu Gupta, Mohan Lal Saxena).
[209:2:2] - **Chandra Shekhar Azad** – the **only** Kakori revolutionary who **escaped and was never caught**.
[209:2:3] TABLE head: Hanged (December 1927) | Jail
  [209:2:3.0] Ram Prasad Bismil (19 Dec) | Gorakhpur
  [209:2:3.1] Ashfaqullah Khan (19 Dec) | Faizabad
  [209:2:3.2] Roshan Singh (19 Dec) | Naini, Allahabad
  [209:2:3.3] Rajendra Lahiri (17 Dec – two days early) | Gonda
[209:2:4] - **Sachindranath Sanyal** – life (second term in the Cellular Jail); **Jogesh Chatterjee** – life.
[209:2:5] - **Bismil** refused milk before his execution: "Now I shall take my **mother's milk** only".
[209:2:6] > NOT in Kakori: **Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru, Surya Sen**.
[209:2:7] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.381-382; PMF Part 4 p.162, p.169-171; NextGen APPSC 06 p.78; en.wikipedia.org Kakori conspiracy (Mulla; Pant in the defence); old app notes (43 arrested, jails, milk)
## SUB 3 | Saunders, the Assembly Bomb and Other Assassinations
[209:3:0] # Saunders (Lahore, 17 December 1928)
[209:3:1] - **Lala Lajpat Rai** died of lathi blows on the **anti-Simon** procession at Lahore (October 1928) → **Bhagat Singh, Azad and Rajguru** shot **ASP J.P. Saunders**, mistaken for **SP James A. Scott**, who ordered the lathi-charge.
[209:3:2] - **Rajguru fired first**, then Bhagat Singh; Azad covered the retreat.
[209:3:3] # Central Legislative Assembly bomb (8 April 1929)
[209:3:4] TABLE head: Particular | Fact
  [209:3:4.0] Who | Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt
  [209:3:4.1] Protest against | Public Safety Bill and Trade Disputes Bill
  [209:3:4.2] Bombs | Deliberately harmless – not to kill but "to make the deaf hear" (leaflet)
  [209:3:4.3] Then | Courted arrest to use the court as a forum for propaganda
  [209:3:4.4] Bhagat Singh's age | a little over 21 (born 28 September 1907)
[209:3:5] - **"Inquilab Zindabad" (Long Live Revolution):** coined by **Maulana Hasrat Mohani** (1921); **Bhagat Singh** first made it the revolutionaries' cry and popularised it – keys give "**Bhagat Singh**" for "who gave / first raised".
[209:3:6] # Other assassinations
[209:3:7] TABLE head: When | Who | Target
  [209:3:7.0] Calcutta, 1924 | Gopinath Saha (hanged) | Charles Tegart, Police Commissioner – shot Ernest Day by mistake
  [209:3:7.1] London, Caxton Hall, 13 March 1940 | Udham Singh | Michael O'Dwyer, Lt. Governor of Punjab at the time of Jallianwala Bagh
[209:3:8] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.382-383; PMF Part 4 p.163, p.140; NextGen APPSC 06 p.67; Rocket Indian History 02 p.93; old app notes (Rajguru first shot, Hasrat Mohani)
## SUB 4 | Chittagong Armoury Raid (18 April 1930) and Bengal
[209:4:0] - **Surya Sen ("Masterda")** – teacher in a national school, **Secretary of the Chittagong District Congress Committee** (1929); planned and led the raid with **Anant (Ananta) Singh, Ganesh Ghosh, Lokenath Bal, Ambika Chakravarty**.
[209:4:1] - Raid of **April 1930** by 65 activists under the banner of the **Indian Republican Army – Chittagong Branch**: seized the armouries, **cut telephone and telegraph lines**, cut the railway link; Sen proclaimed a **Provisional Revolutionary Government**; battle at **Jalalabad Hills**, then guerrilla war.
[209:4:2] - Surya Sen arrested **16 February 1933**, **hanged 12 January 1934**.
[209:4:3] TABLE head: Woman | Action
  [209:4:3.0] Kalpana Dutt(a) | Took part in the raid along with Surya Sen; tried with him – life (not hanged)
  [209:4:3.1] Pritilata Waddedar | Led the attack on the Pahartali European Club (Sept 1932); took cyanide – "Bengal's first woman martyr"
  [209:4:3.2] Santi Ghosh & Suniti Choudhury | Shot the District Magistrate of Comilla (December 1931)
  [209:4:3.3] Bina Das | Fired at Bengal Governor Stanley Jackson while receiving her degree at the convocation (February 1932)
[209:4:4] - New features: **group action** against the colonial state, **women fought with guns**, religious oaths dropped – **Muslims** joined Sen's group.
[209:4:5] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.384-385; PMF Part 4 p.167-168; NextGen APPSC 06 p.78
## SUB 5 | Writings, Ideology and the Naujawan Bharat Sabha
[209:5:0] TABLE head: Work | Author
  [209:5:0.0] Why I am an Atheist (1930, in jail) | Bhagat Singh
  [209:5:0.1] Introduction to Dreamland (book by Lala Ram Saran Das) | Bhagat Singh
  [209:5:0.2] The Cult of the Bomb (*Young India*, 1930) | Mahatma Gandhi – after the bomb under Irwin's train (23 Dec 1929)
  [209:5:0.3] The Philosophy of the Bomb (reply) | Bhagwati Charan Vohra (with Azad and Yashpal)
  [209:5:0.4] Bandi Jivan | Sachindranath Sanyal
  [209:5:0.5] The Indian Struggle | Subhas Chandra Bose
  [209:5:0.6] The Indian Sociologist (journal, London) | Shyamji Krishna Varma – not Bhagat Singh
[209:5:1] - **"Sarfaroshi ki Tamanna ab hamare dil mein hai"** – written by **Bismil Azimabadi**, made famous by **Ram Prasad Bismil** on the way to the gallows (keys: Ram Prasad Bismil).
[209:5:2] - Bhagat Singh: "to be a revolutionary ... one required **criticism and independent thinking**"; revolution "is not the cult of bomb and pistol"; "**by the masses, for the masses**".
[209:5:3] - **Naujawan Bharat Sabha:** founded by **Bhagat Singh** at **Lahore, March 1926**, with **Sukhdev, Bhagwati Charan Vohra**, Yashpal, Chhabil Das – open wing to rouse **youth, peasants and workers**; **opposed communalism**. **Ambika Chakravarti** (Chittagong) was **not** a member.
[209:5:4] - Bhagat Singh's turn to revolution: **Jallianwala Bagh (1919)**, **Nankana Sahib (1921)**, **Chauri Chaura (1922)**.
[209:5:5] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.381, p.386-387; PMF Part 4 p.162, p.165-166, p.170; old app notes (Atheist, Dreamland, Nankana Sahib)
## SUB 6 | Revolutionaries – Birth and Death
[209:6:0] TABLE head: Revolutionary | Born | Death
  [209:6:0.0] Bhagat Singh | 28 September 1907, Banga, Lyallpur district | Hanged 23 March 1931
  [209:6:0.1] Chandrashekhar Azad | 23 July 1906, Bhavra (then Jhabua district, MP; in Alirajpur district since 2008) | Shot himself with his last bullet in a police encounter, Alfred Park, Allahabad, 27 February 1931
  [209:6:0.2] Rajguru (Shivaram Hari) | 1908, Khed (now Rajgurunagar), Maharashtra | Hanged 23 March 1931
  [209:6:0.3] Sukhdev Thapar | 15 May 1907, Ludhiana; taught at the National College, Lahore | Hanged 23 March 1931
  [209:6:0.4] Khudiram Bose | 3 December 1889 | Hanged 1908
  [209:6:0.5] Ram Prasad Bismil | 11 June 1897 | Hanged 19 December 1927, Gorakhpur
[209:6:1] - **APPSC (2024):** all four birth-date pairs (Bhagat Singh, Azad, Khudiram, Bismil) are correct.
[209:6:2] - Azad – "Azad, father Swatantra, home prison" in court; **not hanged**, not executed.
[209:6:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen APPSC 06 p.66-67; PMF Part 4 p.169; en.wikipedia.org Alirajpur district; old app notes (birth dates and places)

=== NOTES 1:210 | Andhra in the Freedom Movement – Alluri Sitarama Raju, Rampa Rebellion, Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
## SUB 0 | Chirala-Perala Movement and Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, 1921
[210:0:0] # Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
[210:0:1] - **Leader** of the **Chirala-Perala movement** (1921) – not Veeraiah Chowdary, Konda Venkatappayya, Prakasam or N.G. Ranga.
[210:0:2] - **Title:** **"Andhra Ratna"** – not Andhra Bhakta, Deshabandhu or Deenabandhu; also called "Ramadasu".
[210:0:3] - **Volunteer corps:** **"Ramadandu"** (1921) – not Shiva Sena, Girisena or Shanti Sena (Shanti Sena = Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary, Pedanandipadu).
[210:0:4] - **Life:** 1884-1929, born at **Penuganchiprolu** (Krishna); M.A. (Hons) Economics, **Edinburgh** (1916); met Gandhi in London (1915), introduced by **Ananda K. Coomaraswamy**.
[210:0:5] - **Education work:** founded the **Andhra Vidyapeetha Goshthi** near Chirala (national education); after the NCM an Andhra secretary of the **Swaraj Party**.
[210:0:6] # The movement
[210:0:7] TABLE head: Angle | Fact
  [210:0:7.0] Place | Chirala and Perala, Bapatla taluk, Guntur district – weavers and small farmers
  [210:0:7.1] Cause | The two villages were made a municipality; yearly tax rose from Rs 4,000 to Rs 40,000
  [210:0:7.2] Method | No-tax campaign (March 1921); Gandhi met Duggirala at the Vijayawada AICC (30-31 March 1921) and visited Chirala on 6 April 1921
  [210:0:7.3] Exodus | Midnight of 25 April 1921: 13,572 of 15,326 residents left their homes
  [210:0:7.4] New township | Ram Nagar (Ramnagar) outside municipal limits, with a parallel all-caste assembly (self-rule); Ramadandu built huts and dug wells; stay lasted 11 months
  [210:0:7.5] Arrest | Duggirala arrested after his speech at the Andhra Mahasabha, Berhampur (Sept-Oct 1921), for breaking a ban on speaking; tried by Rutherford at Srikakulam; one year's rigorous imprisonment
  [210:0:7.6] Failure | Lack of funds (the PCC did not grant even Rs 4,000), rivalry of Konda Venkatappayya and Pattabhi, no leader after his arrest
  [210:0:7.7] Gandhi's view | *Young India*: the municipality meant only more taxes and interference with liberty
  [210:0:7.8] Outcome | Municipality abolished in 1938 by Bezawada Gopala Reddy, minister in the Rajaji ministry
[210:0:8] - Book: ***Chirala Perala Vanavasam*** – **Pisapati Narayana Sastri**.
[210:0:9] - Women: 12 arrested; **first woman jailed – Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma**; Duvvuri Subbamma was also arrested but was not the first.
[210:0:10] > Ramadandu = Duggirala = Chirala-Perala = Andhra Ratna; Ram Nagar = the township of the exodus.
[210:0:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Modern India L3 Part 7 p.5-7; NextGen Modern India L2 Part 6 p.6-7; NextGen previous papers p.2, p.16, p.34, p.38-39; app notes 1:210 (sub 1)
## SUB 1 | Rampa (Manyam) Rebellion, 1922-24
[210:1:0] # Nature and span
[210:1:1] - **Leader and period:** **Alluri Sitarama Raju** (not Aggi Raju, Gantam Dora, Ambul Reddy, Velu Thampi); **1922-1924** (first raid **22 Aug 1922** – Raju shot **7 May 1924**) – not 1919-20, 1921-22 or 1925-26.
[210:1:2] - **Area:** Agency tracts of East Godavari and Visakhapatnam – the **Gudem hills**; base among the **Koya** tribe (with Konda Doras and Konda Reddis) – not Bhils or Gonds.
[210:1:3] - **Character:** armed tribal guerrilla war, **outside the Congress**; caused the British more trouble than the NCM in the region.
[210:1:4] - **Method:** **raided police stations to seize British arms and used them against the British** – not non-cooperation or open war.
[210:1:5] # Chronology and places
[210:1:6] TABLE head: Date | Event
  [210:1:6.0] 22 Aug 1922 | Chintapalli – the first police station attacked (not Rampachodavaram, Krishnadevipeta, Rajavommangi, Annavaram or Addateegala)
  [210:1:6.1] Aug 1922 | Krishnadevipeta and Rajavommangi stations raided
  [210:1:6.2] Sept 1922 | Damanghat / Panjerighat – the first face-to-face battle with the British army; officers Scott Coward and Heiter killed
  [210:1:6.3] 6 Dec 1922 | Peddagaddapalem – first defeat of Raju's forces, a surprise attack by the Malabar Special Police; Raju escaped
  [210:1:6.4] April 1923 | Rebellion resumed – Annavaram police station attacked
  [210:1:6.5] 18 Sept 1923 | Lieutenant Gam Mallu Dora captured – first major setback (so 1923, not 1924)
  [210:1:6.6] 6 May 1924 | Aggi Raju (Pericherla Suryanarayana) captured
  [210:1:6.7] 7 May 1924 | Raju captured and shot at Koyyur
  [210:1:6.8] June 1924 | Gam Gantam Dora killed – end
[210:1:7] # British officers and forces
[210:1:8] TABLE head: Name | Role
  [210:1:8.0] Assam Rifles | Two companies brought in to end the rebellion (paramilitary force) – not "Madras / Malabar / Pune Rifles"
  [210:1:8.1] Rutherford | Special Commissioner appointed to suppress Raju – a civil (colonial) administrator, not an army or Bombay police officer
  [210:1:8.2] Major Goodall | Officer in whose presence (on whose orders) Raju was shot
  [210:1:8.3] Jamedar Kunchu (Kanchu) Menon | Captured Raju
  [210:1:8.4] Bastian | Deputy Tahsildar of Gudem, whose excesses sparked the revolt
[210:1:9] - **Endu Padal** was a follower of Raju from Peddavalasa who wanted to become a muttadar – "Endu Padal – muttadar of Pedda Valasa" is the **wrong pairing**.
[210:1:10] - Associates: **Gam Mallu Dora** (later an MP, 1952), **Gam Gantam Dora**, **Aggi Raju**.
[210:1:11] - **Keirns** arrested Gam Mallu Dora (app notes); the Malabar Special Police were used before the Assam Rifles.
[210:1:12] > First raid = **Chintapalli**; first battle = **Panjerighat**; force that ended it = **Assam Rifles**; Special Commissioner = **Rutherford**.

## SUB 2 | Alluri Sitarama Raju – Life, Death and Memory
[210:2:0] TABLE head: Angle | Fact
  [210:2:0.0] Born | 1897; birthplace in most books and keys Mogallu (Moggallu), West Godavari – other accounts give Pandrangi (near Vizianagaram) or Bhimavaram
  [210:2:0.1] Title | "Manyam Veerudu" (Hero of the Jungle) – not Komaram Bheem or Karam Tammanna Dora
  [210:2:0.2] Training | 1921: visited Chittagong and met Bengal revolutionaries (a British report)
  [210:2:0.3] Stance | Influenced by the NCM but believed in force; not a Congressman
  [210:2:0.4] Death | Captured by Jamedar Kunchu Menon, shot at Koyyur on 7 May 1924 (Major Goodall)
  [210:2:0.5] Burial / tomb | Krishnadevipeta (Visakhapatnam), 8 May 1924 – not Mogallu, Chintapalli or Sankhavaram
  [210:2:0.6] Biographer | Erramalli Narasimha Rao
[210:2:1] - Andhra Patrika (8 May 1924) hailed him as **a great national hero** (exam key).
[210:2:2] - Nickname: **Chittibabu**.
[210:2:3] - Memory: Agency district named **Alluri Sitarama Raju district**; 30-ft statue at **Bhimavaram** for his 125th birth anniversary; **Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram** (Vizianagaram).
[210:2:4] > Born **Mogallu** (exam answer) – shot at **Koyyur** – tomb at **Krishnadevipeta**.

## SUB 3 | Guntur No-Tax Campaigns – Pedanandipadu and Palnadu, 1921-22
[210:3:0] # Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign
[210:3:1] TABLE head: Angle | Fact
  [210:3:1.0] Place | Pedanandipadu firka, Bapatla taluka, Guntur district – "the" no-tax campaign of Andhra (not Chirala, Perala or Nellore)
  [210:3:1.1] Leader | Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary – "Andhra Shivaji"; volunteer force Shanti Sena
  [210:3:1.2] Origin | Grievances of village officers; 18 of 19 village officers resigned (led by Machiraju Ramamurthy); people refused land revenue
  [210:3:1.3] Period | 1921-22 (instalment of Jan-Feb 1922)
  [210:3:1.4] End | Gandhi advised suspension – suspended 11 Feb 1922; ended by March 1922
[210:3:2] - Others: Konda Venkatappayya and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri backed it; **Nyapathi Subbarao** urged restraint; Congress inquiry by **T. Prakasam, Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, Dantu Narayana Raju**; Revenue Board member **L.T. Harris** sent to Guntur; Rutherford's plan to ban the Shanti Sena rejected by the Madras Government.
[210:3:3] # Palnadu forest (Pullari) satyagraha
[210:3:4] - **Pullari** = tax on **grazing cattle in forest lands** (grass tax) – the "Forest Satyagraha", first in **Palnadu** (Guntur).
[210:3:5] - **Period:** **1921-22**. **Leader:** **Kanneganti Hanumanthu**, killed in police firing on **26 Feb 1922** (Minchalapadu).
[210:3:6] - **Unnava Lakshminarayana** went to Palnadu in **July 1921** to study the agitation against the forest laws (not Vedam Venkatachari, Ramadasu Pantulu or Swami Sitaram); arrested with Vedantam Narasimhachari.
[210:3:7] - Social boycott of officials at Macherla.
[210:3:8] - **Shanti Sena** was decided upon by the **Guntur DCC in Dec 1921**; the campaign was suspended after Gandhi's message to Konda Venkatappayya reached the DCC.
[210:3:9] # NCM background in Andhra
[210:3:10] - **Bezawada (Vijayawada) AICC, 31 March - 1 April 1921** brought Gandhi's programme into Andhra; **Delhi AICC (5 Nov 1921)** let provinces start civil disobedience, including no-tax.
[210:3:11] - **"Glorious Decade"** of Andhra = **1921-1931**.
[210:3:12] TABLE head: Place | Movement | Leader
  [210:3:12.0] Chirala-Perala | Against municipal tax | Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
  [210:3:12.1] Palnadu | Pullari / forest satyagraha | Kanneganti Hanumanthu
  [210:3:12.2] Pedanandipadu | No-tax (land revenue) | Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary
  [210:3:12.3] Rampa | Armed tribal rebellion | Alluri Sitarama Raju
[210:3:13] > **Andhra Shivaji** = Parvataneni (Pedanandipadu); Pullari = grazing tax (Palnadu) – not Duggirala.
[210:3:14] ~~ Sources: NextGen Modern India L3 Part 7 p.7-8; NextGen Modern India L2 Part 6 p.6-7; NextGen AP History Part 6 p.12; NextGen previous papers p.1, p.3, p.11, p.26, p.34, p.44, p.58; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.3; Rocket AP History p.29, p.35; app notes 1:210 (sub 2, 3)
## SUB 4 | Agency Grievances and the Earlier Revolts of 1879
[210:4:0] # Grievances behind the Rampa rebellion
[210:4:1] TABLE head: Grievance | Effect
  [210:4:1.0] Madras Forest Act, 1882 | Reserved forests cut podu (shifting cultivation), grazing and forest-produce rights
  [210:4:1.1] Begar | Forced (unpaid) labour for road building – not voluntary or paid labour
  [210:4:1.2] Muttadari system | Extortion by muttadars
  [210:4:1.3] Tahsildar Bastian | Excesses of the local official
[210:4:2] - **Permanent Settlement was not a cause.**
[210:4:3] # 1879 revolts
[210:4:4] - **Rampa revolt (1879-80):** against Mansabdar Madhava Bhupati; leaders Dwarabandala Chandrayya, Ambul Reddy; crushed 1880.
[210:4:5] - **Rekapalli (Rekapalle) revolt (1879):** Bhadrachalam taluk – rising against the **forest laws** and higher taxes on podu after the area joined the Madras Presidency (1874); NextGen's PYQ list puts the 1879 forest revolt at **Chinturu**, a village of the same tract.
[210:4:6] - **Alluri did not lead the 1879-80 revolt** – he was born in 1897.
[210:4:7] - Details (app notes): Rekapalli's spark – axe tax on podu raised from **4 annas to 4-12 annas** in a famine; **Ambul Reddy** is linked with both the Rampa and Rekapalli revolts; **Dwarabandala Chandrayya** burnt the Addateegala police station; **Sullivan** removed Madhava Bhupati and the revolt was crushed in **Nov 1880**.
[210:4:8] TABLE head: Year | Revolt
  [210:4:8.0] 1794 | Vizianagaram – Vijayarama Raju killed at Padmanabham
  [210:4:8.1] 1845-48 | Gulugonda tribal revolt – Chinna Bhupathi
  [210:4:8.2] 1879 | Rampa and Rekapalli revolts
  [210:4:8.3] 1922-24 | Alluri's Rampa rebellion
[210:4:9] > Forest revolt of 1879 = **Rekapalli** (Chinturu in one key); Rampa 1922 = **Forest Act of 1882**.
[210:4:10] ~~ Sources: NextGen Modern India L3 Part 1 p.53; NextGen Modern India L3 Part 7 p.9; NextGen AP History Part 6 p.12; NextGen previous papers p.5-6; app notes 1:210 (sub 4, 5)
## SUB 5 | Andhra Leaders – Titles, Books and Pairings
[210:5:0] TABLE head: Title / work | Person
  [210:5:0.0] Andhra Ratna | Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya
  [210:5:0.1] Andhra Shivaji | Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary
  [210:5:0.2] Andhra Kesari | Tanguturi Prakasam
  [210:5:0.3] Desabhakta | Konda Venkatappayya
  [210:5:0.4] Desoddharaka | Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao (title given at the 1924 Andhra Mahasabha) – not Desabhakta or Desabhimani
  [210:5:0.5] Kavi Raju | Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary
  [210:5:0.6] *Naa Jeevitha Katha* | Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao (autobiography)
  [210:5:0.7] Abhinava Dandi | Ketana – a medieval poet, not a freedom fighter
[210:5:1] - **N.G. Ranga** wrote ***Bapu Blesses***; **Vahini** – a Telugu political journal linked with N.G. Ranga and peasant leaders (Rocket gives 1930).
[210:5:2] - **Ayyanki Venkata Ramanayya** – father of the **library movement** in Andhra.
[210:5:3] - **Kandukuri Veeresalingam** = **Gadya Tikkana**; **Bipin Chandra Pal** = **Vande Mataram** movement (1907 tour of Andhra).
[210:5:4] - **Unnava Lakshminarayana** wrote the novel ***Malapalli*** (written 1921 in Vellore jail, published 1922); ran **Sharada Niketan**, Guntur, with his wife Lakshmibayamma.
[210:5:5] > Match drill: Chirala-Perala – Duggirala; Palnadu – Kanneganti; Rampa – Alluri; library movement – Ayyanki.

=== NOTES 1:211 | Growth of Nationalist Poetry in Telugu – Gurajada, Rayaprolu, Garimella Satyanarayana
## SUB 0 | Patriotic Songs – Poet and Occasion
[211:0:0] TABLE head: Song / line | Poet | Occasion / collection
  [211:0:0.0] "Bharata Khandambu chakkani paadi aavu" | Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham | Improvised while translating Bipin Chandra Pal's Rajahmundry speeches (1907), Vande Mataram movement – India a milch cow milked by the British
  [211:0:0.1] "Maakoddee (Makoddu ye) Tella Doratanamu" | Garimella Satyanarayana | Non-Cooperation movement (first stage, 1921)
  [211:0:0.2] "Veeragandhamu techinaramu, veerulevaro telpudi" | Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary | Civil Disobedience / Salt Satyagraha (1930) – not NCM
  [211:0:0.3] "Kallu Manandoi" | Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri | Civil Disobedience (anti-liquor)
  [211:0:0.4] "Dandalu Dandalu Bharatamata" | Rajahmundry Kesari Samaj | Vijayawada AICC, 1921
  [211:0:0.5] "Desamunu preminchumanna" – "Desamante matti kadoi, desamante manushuloi" | Gurajada Apparao | *Mutyala Saralu* (1910)
  [211:0:0.6] "Ye desamegina ... pogadara nee talli bhoomi Bharatini" (*Janmabhoomi*) | Rayaprolu Subbarao | Patriotic lyric
  [211:0:0.7] "Maa Telugu Talliki mallepoodanda" | Sankarambadi Sundarachari | Later the AP state song
  [211:0:0.8] "Kollayi gattithenemi maa Gandhi" | Basavaraju Apparao | Gandhi song
[211:0:1] - Chilakamarti edited *Desamata*; called the first Telugu national poet ("Andhra Milton").
[211:0:2] - **Rayaprolu Subbarao** is credited (exam key) with first using **"Tenugu talli"** (Mother Telugu) in nationalist verse.
[211:0:3] - Songs in spoken Telugu reached villagers whom pamphlets could not.
[211:0:4] - Firsts (app notes): first Telugu national song **"Hinduvulara ennaallee gati"** (Chilakamarti), who also wrote **"Bharata khandambe okka pedda bandikhana"**; **"The Cry of Mother India"** (Krishna Patrika, 15 Dec 1905) is often called the first nationalist song; C. Narayana Reddy named **"Melukonumi Bharata Putruda"** (Andhra Bharati, 1909); **Yenki paatalu** = Nanduri Subba Rao, not Garimella.
[211:0:5] - Pledge **"Bharata Desam Naa Matrubhoomi"** – **Paidimarri Venkata Subbarao**.
[211:0:6] > Bharata Khandambu = Chilakamarti (1907); Makoddu = Garimella (NCM); Veeragandham = Tripuraneni (Salt Satyagraha).
[211:0:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen Modern India L2 Part 3 p.10, p.13; NextGen Modern India L2 Part 6 p.5-6, p.10; NextGen previous papers p.31; Rocket AP History p.31; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rayaprolu_Subba_Rao; app notes 1:211 (sub 0, 1)
## SUB 1 | Gurajada Apparao
[211:1:0] - **Titles:** **"Abhyudaya Kavitha Pitamahudu"** (father of advanced / progressive poetry), **Kavisekhara**; NextGen: Navayuga Vaitalikudu, Bhava Kavita Vaitalikudu.
[211:1:1] - **Works:** ***Kanyasulkam*** (play on bride-price; written 1892, first staged at **Vizianagaram**), ***Mutyala Saralu*** (1910 poems in his own colloquial metre), *Puttadibomma Purnamma*, *Diddubatu*, *Desabhakti Geyam*; English poem ***Sarangadhara***.
[211:1:2] - Champion of **vyavaharika bhasha** (spoken Telugu) as a literary medium; *Mutyala Saralu* opened modern Telugu poetry.
[211:1:3] - Born at Rayavaram (Visakhapatnam); in the court of Ananda Gajapati of Vizianagaram.
[211:1:4] > "Desamante matti kadoi" is from *Mutyala Saralu* – not *Kanyasulkam*, *Manishi* or *Puttadi Bomma Purnamma*.
[211:1:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen Modern India L2 Part 3 p.9; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.26; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurajada_Apparao; app notes 1:211 (sub 2)
## SUB 2 | Rayaprolu Subbarao and Bhava Kavitvam
[211:2:0] TABLE head: Angle | Fact
  [211:2:0.0] Titles | "Abhinava Nannaya" (Encyclopedia of Indian Literature); Father of Telugu Romanticism
  [211:2:0.1] Contribution | Brought Western (English lyric – Shelley and Keats) romanticism – Bhava Kavitvam – into Telugu; left translations of Sanskrit epics for original, emotive verse
  [211:2:0.2] Works | *Trunakankanamu* (first independent poem), *Andhravali*, *Swatantrya Rathamu*, *Janmabhoomi*, *Misra Manjari* (Sahitya Akademi 1965)
[211:2:1] - **Bhava Kavitvam:** romantic, personal emotion, nature, love; poets Basavaraju Apparao, Duvvuri Ramireddy (*Matru Desa Sankeertanam*), Devulapalli Krishna Sastri (Andhra Shelley), Venkata Parvateeswara Kavulu (*Ekanta Seva*).
[211:2:2] - Progressive writers such as **Sri Sri** called it **"escapist"**.
[211:2:3] > Abhinava Nannaya = **Rayaprolu** (not Viswanatha, Boyi Bhimanna or Sri Sri); Kavi Samrat = Viswanatha.
[211:2:4] ~~ Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rayaprolu_Subba_Rao; NextGen previous papers p.41; app notes 1:211 (sub 3)
## SUB 3 | Garimella Satyanarayana
[211:3:0] TABLE head: Angle | Fact
  [211:3:0.0] Song | "Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu" – Non-Cooperation era; copied a thousand times; praised by Gandhi
  [211:3:0.1] Life | 1893-1952, born at Gonedapadu (Srikakulam); left studies at Gandhi's call
  [211:3:0.2] Jail | Arrested 9 Feb 1922; one year for the song
  [211:3:0.3] Legacy | First people's poet of the freedom struggle; also "Dandalu Dandalu Bharat Mata"
[211:3:1] - *Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu* is **not** his – it is Viswanatha's.
[211:3:2] > "Makoddu ye tella doratanamu" = **Garimella** – not Gurajada, Unnava, Tripuraneni, Dasarathi or Sankarambadi.
[211:3:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen Modern India L2 Part 6 p.5; NextGen previous papers p.31; Rocket AP History p.31; app notes 1:211 (sub 4)
## SUB 4 | Poets' Titles

=== NOTES 1:212 | Revolutionary Literature in Telugu – Sri Sri, Abhyudaya Movement
## SUB 0 | Sri Sri and Mahaprasthanam
[212:0:0] TABLE head: Angle | Fact
  [212:0:0.0] Name | Srirangam Srinivasa Rao (Sri Sri), born 2 Jan 1910, Visakhapatnam
  [212:0:0.1] Key work | *Mahaprasthanam* – poems written 1933-47 (first poem *Jayabheri*, 1933), published 1950; dedicated to Kompella Janardhana Rao
  [212:0:0.2] Preface | Gudipati Venkata Chalam – "Krishna Sastri's pain is the pain of the world; the pain of the world is Sri Sri's pain"
  [212:0:0.3] Title | Mahakavi
  [212:0:0.4] Other works | *Khadga Srushti*, *Maro Prasthanam* (Viplava phase), *Siprali* (Sirisirimuvva satakam and limericks), autobiography *Anantham*; *Gajinche Russia*
  [212:0:0.5] Organisations | Sahiti Samiti (Vizag, with Puripanda Appalaswamy); founding President of Virasam (1970)
  [212:0:0.6] Award | National Award for Best Lyricist – "Telugu Veera Levara" (*Alluri Seetharama Raju*, 1974)
[212:0:1] - Wrote poetry in the **spoken idiom and free verse**; exam key (G1 1994) calls him the first poet to use colloquial Telugu in poetry – strictly Gurajada's *Mutyala Saralu* (1910) came first.
[212:0:2] - Mahaprasthanam is **not** by Arudra, Gopichand or Devulapalli Krishna Sastri.
[212:0:3] > Mahaprasthanam = Sri Sri (1950), preface Chalam; Sri Sri = Mahakavi.
[212:0:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen previous papers p.17; NextGen Modern India L2 Part 8 p.5; NextGen Modern India L3 Part 7 p.12; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurajada_Apparao; app notes 1:212 (sub 2, 3)
## SUB 1 | Gorky's Mother and Leftist Literature in Andhra
[212:1:0] - **Maxim Gorky's *Mother*** was translated into Telugu as ***Amma*** by **Krovvidi (K.) Lingaraju** in **1934** – the work most responsible for **sowing socialism among Andhra youth** (with Sri Sri's *Mahaprasthanam*); not M.S. Ram, Gopichand or C. Rajeswara Rao.
[212:1:1] - Background: failure of the CDM and Nehru's socialist writings turned Andhra youth to the left (Communist Party, Congress Socialist Party, M.N. Roy's Radical Humanists).
[212:1:2] - **Andhra Socialist Party:** June 1934, Vijayawada – N.G. Ranga president, Madduri Annapurnayya secretary; members included K. Lingaraju, P. Sundarayya, C. Rajeswara Rao.
[212:1:3] - Leftist journals: *Udayini* (Kompella Janardhana Rao), *Pratibha* (Siva Sankara Sastri); Rayalaseema – *Navya Sahityamala*.
[212:1:4] - Publishers: **Adarsha Grantha Mandali – Gadde Lingayya**; **Viswa Sahityamala – Mahidhara brothers**.
[212:1:5] - **Tenali** radicals (M.N. Roy): **T. Gopichand** – ***Asamarthuni Jeevitha Yatra*** (1947), first psychological novel in Telugu (not N.G. Ranga, Sri Sri or K. Lingaraju); *Pandita Parameswara Sastri Veelunama* – Sahitya Akademi; first Director of Information, Andhra State (1953).
[212:1:6] > Amma (1934) = Krovvidi Lingaraju; *Parivarthana*, *Mundadugu*, *Maa Bhoomi* are distractors.
[212:1:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen Modern India L3 Part 7 p.12; NextGen Modern India L2 Part 8 p.5; NextGen previous papers p.11, p.23, p.30; app notes 1:212 (sub 4, 6)
## SUB 2 | Arasam, AIPWA and Virasam
[212:2:0] TABLE head: Body | Year / place | Note
  [212:2:0.0] AIPWA (All India Progressive Writers' Association) | 1936, Lucknow | Founding session presided by Premchand; president in 2011: Namvar Singh (exam key)
  [212:2:0.1] Arasam (Abhyudaya Rachayitala Sangham) | 1943; first conference Tenali | Telugu counterpart of the AIPWA; first conference presided by Tapi Dharma Rao
  [212:2:0.2] Virasam (Viplava Rachayitala Sangham) | July 1970, Hyderabad | Revolutionary Writers' Association; founding President Sri Sri; Vice-President Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao
[212:2:1] - Path: **nationalist poetry → Abhyudaya (progressive, Arasam) → Viplava (revolutionary, Virasam, after Srikakulam)**.
[212:2:2] - Virasam's spark: **Sri Sri's Shashtipurti, Vizag, Feb 1970**; its publications ***Le*** and ***March*** were banned.
[212:2:3] - Virasam is **not** the "Progressive Writers' Association" – that is Arasam.
[212:2:4] > Arasam 1943 = progressive; Virasam 1970 = revolutionary.
[212:2:5] ~~ Sources: app notes 1:212 (sub 0, 1)
## SUB 3 | Abhyudaya Writers and Titles
[212:3:0] TABLE head: Writer | Works / title
  [212:3:0.0] Arudra (Bhagavatula Sadasiva Sankara Sastri; Sri Sri's nephew) | *Tvamevaham* (Telangana struggle), *Samagra Andhra Sahityam*; translated *Veera Telangana Viplava Geethalu*
  [212:3:0.1] Boyi Bhimanna | *Gudisale Kalipotunnayi* (Sahitya Akademi 1975); also "Mahakavi"
  [212:3:0.2] Kundurti Anjaneyulu | "Vachana Kavitha Pitamaha"; *Kundurti Kritulu* (Sahitya Akademi 1977)
  [212:3:0.3] Kodavatiganti Kutumba Rao | *Chaduvu* (1952); editor of *Chandamama*
  [212:3:0.4] Gunturu Seshendra Sarma | "Yuga Kavi"
  [212:3:0.5] Gurram Jashuva | *Gabbilam*, *Firdausi*; "Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti"; called "Poet of the Millennium" (Wikipedia)
  [212:3:0.6] Viswanatha Satyanarayana | "Kavi Samrat" – a traditionalist, not an Abhyudaya poet
  [212:3:0.7] Jwalamukhi | One of the six Digambara poets (1965) – not Bhava or Pracheena Kavi
[212:3:1] - Traditionalists said Sri Sri's free verse destroyed the "sweetness" of Telugu.
[212:3:2] > Poet of the Millennium = **Jashuva** (Wikipedia; one key gives Sri Sri); Maha Kavi = Sri Sri; Yuga Kavi = Seshendra.
[212:3:3] ~~ Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gurram_Jashuva; app notes 1:212 (sub 4, 5)
## SUB 4 | Praja Natya Mandali and Progressive Theatre
[212:4:0] - **Praja Natya Mandali (1943):** communist cultural front, **Andhra wing of IPTA**; spread ideas through drama, songs and folk forms – main form **Burrakatha**; workshops by Garikapati Rajarao and Koduri Atchaiah; suspended by 1948.
[212:4:1] - Play ***Maa Bhoomi*** – **Sunkara Satyanarayana and Vasireddy Bhaskara Rao**.
[212:4:2] - **Jana Natya Mandali (1971):** grew from the Art Lovers (1970) of **Gaddar and B. Narsinga Rao** – Viplava phase.
[212:4:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen Modern India L2 Part 8 p.5; app notes 1:212 (sub 7)

=== NOTES 1:214 | Women in the National Movement in Andhra – Durgabai Deshmukh, Unnava Lakshmibayamma, Duvvuri Subbamma
## SUB 0 | Durgabai Deshmukh
[214:0:0] # Early role (NCM)
[214:0:1] - **April 1921, Kakinada:** the young Durgabai **translated Gandhi's speech into Telugu**, collected **Rs 5,000** and arranged his meeting with **Devadasis and Muslim women**.
[214:0:2] - As a volunteer she **stopped Jawaharlal Nehru at the gate** for having no pass (accounts place it at the Vijayawada AICC 1921 or the Kakinada Congress 1923).
[214:0:3] - **CDM:** broke the salt law in **Madras city** with T. Prakasam and K. Nageswara Rao.
[214:0:4] # Institutions, titles, awards
[214:0:5] TABLE head: Angle | Fact
  [214:0:5.0] Andhra Mahila Sabha | Founded by Durgabai in Madras, 1937 (APPSC 2023 stem: 1938) – women's education and welfare; not Sarojini Naidu or Duvvuri Subbamma
  [214:0:5.1] Journal | Telugu monthly *Andhra Mahila*
  [214:0:5.2] Book | *The Stone that Speaketh*
  [214:0:5.3] Titles | "Andhra Mahila", "Iron Lady (of Andhra)"; honorary doctorate from Andhra University
  [214:0:5.4] After 1947 | Member of the Constituent Assembly
  [214:0:5.5] Social welfare | First chairperson, Central Social Welfare Board (1953); CSWB later registered under Section 25, Indian Companies Act 1956
  [214:0:5.6] Awards | Paul G. Hoffman award; Padma Vibhushan (1975) – not 1965
  [214:0:5.7] Born | 1909
[214:0:6] - **APPSC 2023 (withdrawn):** "Andhra Aatmiya Sabha" is false – the **Atmiya Sabha (1815)** was Ram Mohan Roy's; no option fitted.
[214:0:7] - **Devarakonda (1931) Andhra Mahila Sabha** of the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha (T. Varalakshmamma) is a different body.
[214:0:8] > Trap: Andhra Mahila Sabha = Durgabai; Padma Vibhushan = 1975.
[214:0:9] ~~ Sources: app notes 1:214 (sub 1, 2); NextGen AP History Part 22 p.27; PMF Modern History 03 p.163
## SUB 1 | Maganti Annapurnamma and Gandhi's 1921 Tour
[214:1:0] - **Gandhi's 1921 coastal tour** (Kakinada, Rajahmundry, Eluru, Vijayawada, Chirala, Nellore) **drew women into the struggle**; he collected the **Tilak Swaraj Fund**.
[214:1:1] - **Maganti Annapurnamma** (Eluru, wife of **Maganti Bapineedu**): **first Telugu woman to give all her jewellery to the Tilak Swaraj Fund** and **burn foreign goods**; first to **give up foreign cloth and wear khaddar** during Gandhi's visit.
[214:1:2] - **Yamini Purna Tilakam:** a **dancer (devadasi)** who gave her **entire property** to the fund and followed Gandhi – "as Amrapali followed the Buddha".
[214:1:3] - **Women leaders of the NCM:** Duvvuri Subbamma, Ponaka Kanakamma, Unnava Lakshmibayamma – orators and organisers.
[214:1:4] > Repeat (×7): first jewels / first khaddar = **Maganti Annapurnamma**, not Durgabai or Ponaka Kanakamma.
[214:1:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 7 p.14, Part 18 p.28, Part 22 p.21; app notes 1:214 (sub 0, 5)
## SUB 2 | Unnava Couple and Sarada Niketanam
[214:2:0] - **Sri Sarada Niketanam, Guntur:** founded by **Unnava Lakshminarayana** with his wife **Unnava Lakshmibayamma** (G2 2019 key: Lakshminarayana).
[214:2:1]   - **1902:** the couple ran a **widow asylum**; she held its first widow remarriage. **1922:** Women's Gurukulam, into which the asylum merged.
[214:2:2]   - She ran the monthly **Sri Sarada Niketanam**.
[214:2:3] - **Unnava Lakshminarayana** wrote the novel ***Malapalli***; he went to **Palnadu (July 1921)** to study the forest (pullari) satyagraha and was arrested.
[214:2:4] - **Guntur hartal:** after his arrest, Lakshmibayamma led the Guntur hartals with **Yamini Purna Tilakam**.
[214:2:5] - **Salt Satyagraha, 9 April 1930:** Lakshmibayamma and Rukmini Lakshmipathi led the women of **Krishna and Guntur**.
[214:2:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 7 p.26, Part 19 p.27; app notes 1:214 (sub 3)
## SUB 3 | Duvvuri Subbamma and the Salt Satyagraha Women
[214:3:0] TABLE head: Woman | Distinctive fact
  [214:3:0.0] Duvvuri Subbamma | Title "Desabandhavi"; first Andhra woman jailed (first in India: Parvati Devi of Punjab); national school Sanatana Vidyalayam, Rajahmundry; made salt at Chollangi (6 April 1930) → Nellore jail; lathi charge at Peddapuram (QIM 1942)
  [214:3:0.1] Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi | First woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha (Vedaranyam, 1930); APPSC key: first woman graduate of Andhra
  [214:3:0.2] Khammampati Manikyamba | Jailed in the Salt Satyagraha with her six-month-old baby
  [214:3:0.3] Durgabai Deshmukh | Salt Satyagraha in Madras city; Constituent Assembly
  [214:3:0.4] Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy | Presided the first Andhra Rashtra Mahila Mahasabha (APPSC match)
  [214:3:0.5] Ravuri Alivelu Mangatayaramma | One of 12 women jailed at Chirala-Perala (1921)
  [214:3:0.6] Chitturi Annapurna Devi | Arrested at 17 for distributing pamphlets, QIM (Guntur)
[214:3:1] - Other CDM women jailed: **Bharati Devi Ranga**, Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmamma, Digumarti Janakamma.
[214:3:2] > Match (APPSC): Muthulakshmi – Mahila Mahasabha; Durgabai – Constituent Assembly; Rukmini – Vedaranyam; Subbamma – Desabandhavi.
[214:3:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 22 p.27; app notes 1:214 (sub 4, 5, 6)

=== NOTES 1:215 | Prominent Andhra Leaders – Konda Venkatappayya, Pattabhi Sitaramayya, Tanguturi Prakasam, Bulusu Sambamurthy
## SUB 0 | Tanguturi Prakasam – Andhra Kesari
[215:0:0] # Simon boycott, 1928
[215:0:1] - Simon Commission appointed **Nov 1927**, arrived **3 Feb 1928**.
[215:0:2] - In the **Simon Go Back** protest at **Madras (1928)** Prakasam **bared his chest before police guns** ("shoot me") → title **"Andhra Kesari"** – not Home Rule, Vande Mataram or Quit India.
[215:0:3] # Papers and career
[215:0:4] TABLE head: Year | Fact
  [215:0:4.0] 1872 | Born 23 Aug 1872, Vinodarayunipalem (NextGen prints 1892, Valluru – wrong)
  [215:0:4.1] 1903 | Chairman, Rajahmundry Municipality; acted main roles in the Hindu Nataka Samajam
  [215:0:4.2] 1921 | Gave up law practice for the NCM (not 1925); started the English daily *Swarajya* (26 Oct 1921); also weekly *Grama Swarajya*
  [215:0:4.3] 1937 | Revenue Minister in Rajaji's ministry – pro-peasant zamindari enquiry, opposed inside his party
  [215:0:4.4] 1946 | Premier of composite Madras; Firka Development Scheme
  [215:0:4.5] 1951 | Left Congress with N.G. Ranga → Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party
  [215:0:4.6] 1953 | First Chief Minister of Andhra State (Bezawada Gopal Reddy 2nd and last)
[215:0:5] - President of the Andhra Congress Committee **18 times**; **Prakasam district** is named after him.
[215:0:6] - Books: autobiography ***Naa Jeevita Yatra*** (4th part by **Tenneti Viswanatham**); ***Law Times***.
[215:0:7] - **Prakasam district irrigation:** **Gundlakamma Reservoir** (also Veligonda).
[215:0:8] > Trap: Swarajya = English daily; "Kesari" is only his title.
[215:0:9] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 7 p.3-4, p.11, p.23, p.28; Part 19 p.5; app notes 1:215 (sub 4)
## SUB 1 | Konda Venkatappayya and the Andhra Congress Circle
[215:1:0] TABLE head: Year | Role
  [215:1:0.0] 1866 | Born 22 Feb, Guntur; a lawyer
  [215:1:0.1] 1902 | Co-founded *Krishna Patrika* with Dasu Narayana Rao; its first editor (Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited it later)
  [215:1:0.2] 1907 / 1910 | President, Tenali Swadeshi meeting / National College, Machilipatnam
  [215:1:0.3] 1913 | Secretary, first Andhra Mahasabha, Bapatla
  [215:1:0.4] 1917 | President, fifth Andhra Mahasabha, Nellore
  [215:1:0.5] 1918 | Secretary of the Andhra Congress Circle (22 Jan 1918) – its first President was Nyapathi Subba Rao
  [215:1:0.6] 1920 | Opposed the NCM resolution at the Calcutta special session
  [215:1:0.7] 1923 | AICC Secretary
  [215:1:0.8] 1930 | Dictator of the Civil Disobedience (Salt) Satyagraha in Andhra
[215:1:1] - Title **"Desabhakta"**; called the **Father of the Andhra (State) Movement**; book ***Andhrudyamam***.
[215:1:2] - **⚠ Disputed:** APPSC G2 2011 keyed Konda as first president of the Andhra Congress Circle; NextGen and the 1918 record give **Nyapathi Subba Rao**.
[215:1:3] > Trap: Konda = Secretary at Bapatla (1913) and in 1918; President at Nellore (1917).
[215:1:4] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 6 p.4, p.12; Part 7 p.4, p.9; Part 22 p.27; Wikipedia N._Subba_Rao_Pantulu; app notes 1:215 (sub 3)
## SUB 2 | Pattabhi Sitaramayya
[215:2:0] - **Andhra Bank (1923, Machilipatnam)**; also Krishna District Co-operative Bank, **Bharata Lakshmi Bank**, Andhra Insurance – the patriot who was also a great **businessman**.
[215:2:1] - Books: ***History of the Indian National Congress* (1935)** – the **official history** of the Congress; ***Feathers and Stones*** (Ahmednagar Fort diary); *Gandhi and Gandhism*.
[215:2:2] - **Tripuri (1939):** Gandhi's candidate, **defeated by Subhas Chandra Bose** – Gandhi called it "my own defeat".
[215:2:3] - Presided the **Jaipur session (1948)**; member of the **JVP Committee** (Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi) – it first **rejected** linguistic states (report **April 1949**).
[215:2:4] - Wrote in *The Hindu* on the need for **linguistic states**; APCC President (1937).
[215:2:5] - **Governor of Madhya Pradesh (1952-57)**.
[215:2:6] - First Telugu INC president: exam keys say **Pattabhi**; strictly **P. Ananda Charlu** presided in 1891.
[215:2:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 7 p.9, Part 19 p.24; app notes 1:215 (sub 5)
## SUB 3 | Titles of Andhra Leaders

  [215:3:0.6] Andhra Sivaji | Parvataneni Veerayya Chowdary
  [215:3:0.7] Andhra Tilak | Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao (named the Ceded Districts Rayalaseema)
  [215:3:0.8] Desoddharaka | Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao

## SUB 4 | Bulusu Sambamurthy and the Sribagh Pact
[215:4:0] - **Bulusu Sambamurthy ("Maharshi"):** backed the 1920 election boycott; attended the Vijayawada AICC (1921); **Reception Committee chairman, Kakinada session (1923)**; **toured all Andhra** for the Simon boycott (1928).
[215:4:1] - **Speaker of the Madras Assembly** in the **first Rajaji ministry (1937)**; declared Andhra state must be formed before the Constitution came into force.
[215:4:2] - **Potti Sriramulu's fast** began **19 Oct 1952** at **Sambamurthy's house in Mylapore, Madras**; Sriramulu died 15 Dec 1952.
[215:4:3] - **Sribagh Pact, 16 Nov 1937:** Rayalaseema–Circar agreement at **Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's house "Sribagh"**, Madras; coastal signatories **Prakasam and Sambamurthy**.
[215:4:4] - Tirupati question (1953): the keyed answer credits **C. Rajagopalachari** with keeping Tirupati in Andhra against the Tamil claim (unverified).
[215:4:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 6 p.13, Part 7 p.17, p.23, Part 23 p.14; app notes 1:215 (sub 6)
## SUB 5 | Pingali Venkayya
[215:5:0] - Born **2 Aug 1876**, **Bhatlapenumarru** (near Machilipatnam).
[215:5:1] - **Soldier in the British Army in South Africa (Anglo-Boer War)**.
[215:5:2] - Attended the **Calcutta INC session (1906)**; 1916 book ***Bharatha Desaniki Oka Jatiya Patakam*** (about 30 flag designs).
[215:5:3] - Showed his flag to Gandhi at the **Vijayawada AICC (31 Mar – 1 Apr 1921)**.
[215:5:4] - Titles: **Patti** (cotton varieties), **Japan**, **Diamond** Venkayya.
[215:5:5] ~~ Sources: app notes 1:215 (sub 7)

=== NOTES 1:216 | Peasant Movements – Indigo, Deccan Riots, Moplah, Bardoli, Tebhaga, Telangana Armed Struggle
## SUB 0 | Indigo Revolt, Nil Darpan, Pabna and the Deccan Riots
[216:0:0] # Indigo Revolt (1859-60), Bengal
[216:0:1] - European planters forced ryots to grow **indigo instead of paying crops like rice**, through **advances and fraudulent contracts**, at prices that did not pay; intimidation, flogging, seizure of cattle.
[216:0:2] - Leaders **Digambar and Bishnu Biswas** of **Nadia**; ryots refused to sow, went on rent strike and used the courts.
[216:0:3] - **Supported by the Bengali intelligentsia** – press (**Harish Chandra Mukherjee's *Hindoo Patriot***), meetings, legal aid; missionaries too.
[216:0:4] - **Indigo Commission (March 1860):** found planters coercive; ryots must **fulfil existing contracts** but **could refuse future ones**; Nov 1860 notification – no compulsion. It did **not** find indigo profitable to ryots.
[216:0:5] - Came **immediately after 1857** (Sanyasi 1763-1800 and Santhal 1855-56 earlier; Pabna 1873-76 later).
[216:0:6] # Nil Darpan
[216:0:7] TABLE head: Role | Person
  [216:0:7.0] Written (Bengali play, 1860) | Dinabandhu Mitra
  [216:0:7.1] English translation | Michael Madhusudan Dutt
  [216:0:7.2] Published | Rev. James Long
[216:0:8] - Nil Darpan (1860) is earlier than Satyendranath Tagore's ICS (1863), Arya Samaj (1875) and Anandamath (1882).
[216:0:9] - **Tinkathia** (indigo on **3/20** of land) belongs to **Champaran (Bihar, 1917)**, ended by the Champaran Agrarian Act 1918.
[216:0:10] # Pabna and Deccan
[216:0:11] - **Pabna (1873-76):** agrarian league of **Ishan Chandra Roy and Shambhu Pal** against **rent hikes** by zamindars; legal, peaceful → **Bengal Tenancy Act 1885**.
[216:0:12] - **Deccan Riots (1875):** **Poona and Ahmednagar**; ryotwari peasants vs **Marwari and Gujarati moneylenders**; debt bonds burnt; cause incl. the **Limitation Law of 1859** → **Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act 1879** (protection from **moneylenders**).
[216:0:13] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.607-609; PMF Modern History 03 p.120-121; app notes 1:216 (sub 1, 2)
## SUB 1 | Peasant Movements – Chronology and Regions
[216:1:0] TABLE head: Movement | Year | Region
  [216:1:0.0] Sanyasi Revolt | 1763-1800 | Bengal (after the 1770 famine)
  [216:1:0.1] Santhal Rebellion | 1855-56 | Rajmahal hills – before 1857
  [216:1:0.2] Indigo Revolt | 1859-60 | Bengal (Nadia)
  [216:1:0.3] Pabna | 1873-76 | East Bengal
  [216:1:0.4] Deccan Riots | 1875 | Poona-Ahmednagar
  [216:1:0.5] Bijolia | 1897-1927 | Mewar – Sitaram Das, then Vijay Singh Pathik
  [216:1:0.6] Birsa Munda ulgulan | 1899-1900 | Bihar (Chotanagpur)
  [216:1:0.7] Champaran / Kheda | 1917 / 1918 | Bihar / Gujarat (Patel, Mohanlal Pandya)
  [216:1:0.8] Eka | 1921-22 | Awadh (UP)
  [216:1:0.9] Moplah | 1921 | Malabar (Kerala)
  [216:1:0.10] Bardoli | 1928 | Surat district, Gujarat
  [216:1:0.11] Tebhaga | 1946-47 | Bengal
  [216:1:0.12] Telangana | 1946-51 | Hyderabad State – not Malabar
[216:1:1] - **After 1857:** Indigo, Deccan riots, Birsa Munda – **not** Santhal (UPPCS 2017).
[216:1:2] - **Match (UPSC 1997):** Moplah – Kerala, Pabna – Bengal, Eka – Awadh, Birsa – Bihar.
[216:1:3] - **Phases:** sporadic revolts (pre-1917) → **Gandhian satyagraha** (Champaran, Kheda, Bardoli) → organised **Kisan Sabhas** and Left-led struggles.
[216:1:4] - **Permanent Settlement (1793)** made zamindars **proprietors** and cultivators tenants – the root of anti-zamindari struggles.
[216:1:5] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.607-615; app notes 1:216 (sub 0)
## SUB 2 | Kisan Sabhas, Swami Sahajanand and the AIKS
[216:2:0] TABLE head: Body | Fact
  [216:2:0.0] Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha | Formed 1929 by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati; joined by Karyanand Sharma, Yadunandan Sharma, Rahul Sankrityayan
  [216:2:0.1] All India Kisan Sabha | April 1936, Lucknow – president Sahajanand, general secretary N.G. Ranga; Kisan Manifesto (Aug 1936): zamindari abolition, debt cancellation; red flag adopted Oct 1937
  [216:2:0.2] AIKS 8th session | 1944, Vijayawada – presided by Sahajanand Saraswati
[216:2:1] - **Bakasht movement (Bihar):** demand to **return bakasht land** taken by zamindars from tenants – led by **Karyanand Sharma**; **Barahiya Tal (Munger)** was its centre.
[216:2:2] - Sahajanand = **peasant (Kisan Sabha) movement in Bihar** in the 1930s – not tribal, labour or caste.
[216:2:3] ~~ Sources: PMF Modern History 05 p.142-145; Spectrum p.613-614
## SUB 3 | UP Kisan Sabha, Awadh and the Eka Movement
[216:3:0] TABLE head: Body | Year | Leaders | Issue
  [216:3:0.0] UP Kisan Sabha | Feb 1918 | Gauri Shankar Mishra, Indra Narayan Dwivedi; backed by M.M. Malaviya | Peasant grievances – not Nehru
  [216:3:0.1] Awadh (Oudh) Kisan Sabha | Oct 1920 | Jawaharlal Nehru, Baba Ramchandra | Rent hikes, bedakhali, begar (unpaid forced labour)
  [216:3:0.2] Eka (unity) | 1921-22 | Madari Pasi and low-caste leaders | Rents 50% above recorded, thikadars, share-rents
[216:3:1] - Eka began in **Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur** (also Barabanki) – keyed aim: **conversion of produce rent into cash**.
[216:3:2] - **Eka vs Bardoli (UPSC 2026):** Bardoli fought a **30% hike in land revenue**; Eka fought **high rents** of taluqdars and turned violent, outside Congress control.
[216:3:3] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.610-611; app notes 1:216 (sub 3)
## SUB 4 | Telangana Armed Struggle (1946-51)
[216:4:0] - Against the **Nizam's feudal order** – deshmukhs, jagirdars, **vetti** (forced labour); led by the **CPI** through the **Andhra Mahasabha** – the biggest peasant guerrilla war (3,000 villages).
[216:4:1] - Land redistributed; **village soviets** set up; **called off October 1951**.
[216:4:2] - **Doddi Komaraiah:** **first martyr** – shot at **Kadavendi** (Jangaon taluka, Nalgonda) on **4 July 1946** by the **Visnur deshmukh's** men while **defending a poor washerwoman's land** (**Chakali Ailamma**).
[216:4:3] - Leaders: **P. Sundarayya, Chandra Rajeswara Rao**; woman fighter **Mallu Swarajyam**; Andhra Mahasabha president 1941-46 **M. Suryanarayana**; **Ravi Narayana Reddy** presided Chilkur (1941); 11th session **Bhongir (1944)** communist-dominated.
[216:4:4] TABLE head: Book | Author
  [216:4:4.0] *Veera Telangana – Naa Anubhavalu, Gnapakalu* (Heroic Telangana) | Ravi Narayana Reddy – not Mallu Swarajyam
  [216:4:4.1] *History of the People's Armed Struggle of Telangana (1946-51)* | Devulapalli Venkateswara Rao (NextGen/APPSC line: "Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao")
  [216:4:4.2] *Telangana People's Struggle and its Lessons* | P. Sundarayya
[216:4:5] - **Vetti vs bonded labour:** vetti = caste-bound forced service of village servant castes; bonded labour = debt-based, regardless of caste (the statements swap them).
[216:4:6] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.615-616; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.4, p.8, Part 19 p.16; Wikipedia D._V._Rao; app notes 1:216 (sub 6, 9)
## SUB 5 | Moplah Revolt (1921) and Bardoli (1928)
[216:5:0] - **Moplah (Mappila):** **Muslim tenants of Malabar** against **Hindu landlords (jenmis)** and the British – no security of tenure, high rents, renewal fees; merged with the **Khilafat** agitation; arrest of **Ali Musliyar** (Aug 1921); leader **Variyankunnath Kunjahammad Haji**.
[216:5:1] - **Wagon Tragedy, November 1921:** Moplah prisoners suffocated in a closed railway wagon.
[216:5:2] - **Bardoli (Surat, Gujarat):** against a **30% land-revenue hike**; **Vallabhbhai Patel** – women gave him the title **"Sardar"**; inquiry cut the hike to 6.03%.
[216:5:3] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.611-612; app notes 1:216 (sub 4)
## SUB 6 | Tebhaga Movement (1946-47)
[216:6:0] - Call of the **Bengal Provincial Kisan Sabha (Sept 1946)** to implement the **Floud Commission's** tebhaga: **two-thirds of the crop to the bargadar** instead of one-half – the landlord's share cut **from one-half to one-third**.
[216:6:1] - **Bargadars / adhiars** (sharecroppers) against **jotedars**; slogan "take the paddy to our own threshing floor".
[216:6:2] - Outcome: **Bargadari Bill / Act (1950)**.
[216:6:3] ~~ Sources: Spectrum p.615; app notes 1:216 (sub 5)
## SUB 7 | N.G. Ranga and the Kisan Movement in Andhra
[216:7:0] TABLE head: Year | Event
  [216:7:0.0] 1923 | Agricultural Labourers' Mahasabha, Nidubrolu
  [216:7:0.1] 1928 | Andhra Provincial Ryots' Association – N.G. Ranga
  [216:7:0.2] 1933 | Ryot agitation led by Parvataneni Veeriah Chowdary
  [216:7:0.3] 1933-34 | First Kisan School (Indian Peasants' Institute) at Nidubrolu, Guntur – with his brothers and wife Bharathi Devi
  [216:7:0.4] May 1938 | Andhra Rythu Vidyalayam, Madanapalle (T.N. Ramakrishna Reddy)
  [216:7:0.5] 1939 | Rajakeeya Pathashala (School of Politics), Kankipadu
[216:7:1] > Trap: Nidubrolu = first Kisan school; Kankipadu = School of Politics.
[216:7:2] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 7 p.8; Spectrum p.614; PMF Modern History 05 p.142; app notes 1:216 (sub 7)

## SUB 1 | N.G. Ranga – Founder of the Andhra Kisan Movement
[218:1:0] TABLE head: Angle | Fact
  [218:1:0.0] Name | Gogineni Ranganayakulu – "Acharya" N.G. Ranga
  [218:1:0.1] Born | 7 Nov 1900, Nidubrolu (Guntur)
  [218:1:0.2] Titles | Rythu Bandhu / Rythu Bandhava; "Father of the Indian Peasant Movement"; founder of the Kisan movement in Andhra (G2 2011, 2019)

  [218:1:0.4] 1933 | Led the historic Ryot Agitation of Andhra (1933); farmers' movement in Venkatagiri 1933-36
  [218:1:0.5] Guntur | Organised the first farmers' (ryots') association in Guntur
  [218:1:0.6] Institutions | Indian Peasants Institute / first Kisan School, Nidubrolu (1933-34); Rajakeeya Pathashala ("School of Politics"), Kankipadu, 1939
  [218:1:0.7] Other | 1929 memorandum to the Whitley Commission – minimum wages; Andhra Socialist Party (1934); Krishikar Lok Party (1951); Swatantra Party (1959)
  [218:1:0.8] Honour | Padma Vibhushan (1991), not Bharat Ratna
  [218:1:0.9] Journals | Praja Bandhu, Navayuga (also Chitragupta)
  [218:1:0.10] Books | Credo of World Peasantry, Revolutionary Peasantry, Fight for Freedom, Bapu Blesses

## SUB 3 | Ryots' Associations and the 1937 Rythu Rakshana Yatra
[218:3:0] - **Krishna District Rythu Sangham (1915)**; Guntur and Godavari sanghams (1923).
[218:3:1] - **Andhra Provincial Ryots Association / Andhra Rashtra Rythu Sangham – 1928**, started by **N.G. Ranga** (with **Narasimha Devara Satyanarayana, Maganti Bapineedu**); first General Secretary **B.V. Ratnam** (not a founder); **merged into the AIKS in 1936**.
[218:3:2] - Nellore: Nellore Zilla Zamindari Rytu Sangam (Dodla Ramireddy, 1929); Zamin Rytu Sangam (Vennalkanti Raghavaiah, 1930) – paper '**Zamin Rytu**'.
[218:3:3] - Visakhapatnam Peasant Mahasabha (**1929**) – first in North Coastal Andhra; paper **Prajavani**.
[218:3:4] # Rythu Rakshana Yatra (1937)
[218:3:5] - **Ichchapuram → Madras**; **launched by Ranga on 3 July 1937**, **led on the ground by Kommareddi Satyanarayana**.
[218:3:6] - Compared to the **Dandi March**; ended with a memorandum to **Speaker Bulusu Sambamurthy** (Prakasam was Revenue Minister).
[218:3:7] - NextGen also dates a Ranga cycle rally Itchapuram → Madras to **1938-39** (against the Madras Land Settlement Act).
[218:3:8] ~~ Sources: PMF Modern History Part 5 p.145; NextGen AP History Part 19 p.11-12, p.15, p.5; old app notes (founders, B.V. Ratnam, yatra details)
## SUB 4 | Munagala Paragana Struggle (1930s)
[218:4:0] - **Location:** **Nandigama taluk, Krishna district** then; now **Suryapet (earlier Nalgonda)**, Telangana.
[218:4:1] - **Zamindar:** **Nayani Venkata Ranga Rao** (Keesaravari family) – literary patron but a harsh landlord.
[218:4:2] - Bodies: Munagala Peasant Association (Batchala Jagannadh Das); Zamin Peasant Association (**Kodati Venkata Narasimha Rao**).
[218:4:3] - **Kalukova Satyagraha (1938)** – **Nanduri Prasada Rao**, over a paddy wage of 80 seers per acre.
[218:4:4] - **Brahmaiah Award (15 Jan 1939)** – by APCC Secretary **Gottipati Brahmaiah**; settlement covering **142 villages**.
[218:4:5] - **Munagala Day: 11 June 1939**; agitation **withdrawn 19 June 1939** after Prakasam and Ranga promised action.
[218:4:6] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 19 p.11-12; old app notes (142 villages, Munagala Day, withdrawal)
