## SUB 6 | Secularism, the Hindu Code and Language
[254:6:0] - Indian secularism: **no State religion**; the State is neutral but **may intervene to reform social practices** (unlike strict Western separation).
[254:6:1] - **Art. 30** – minority educational institutions; **Art. 343** – Hindi in Devanagari, English to continue for **15 years**.
[254:6:2] - **Ambedkar** – first **Law Minister** (1947); resigned **27 Sep 1951** over the stalled **Hindu Code Bill**.
[254:6:3] - **Hindu Marriage Act 1955**; Succession, Minority and Guardianship, Adoptions and Maintenance Acts **1956**.
[254:6:4] ~~ Sources: Spectrum Modern India p.237 (Hindu Marriage Act 1955); old app notes row 254

=== NOTES 1:255 | Andhra Movement, Potti Sriramulu's Fast and the Formation of Andhra State, 1953
## SUB 0 | The First Andhra Conference (Andhra Mahasabha), Bapatla 1913
[255:0:0] # Before Bapatla
[255:0:1] TABLE head: Meeting | Place, year | Key point
  [255:0:1.0] Youngmen's Literary Association | Guntur, 1903 | Cradle of the Andhra movement
  [255:0:1.1] Joint conference of Godavari, Krishna, Guntur districts | Nidadavolu, May 1912 | Andhra province issue first discussed in the Subjects Committee (21st Krishna-Guntur conference); first formal separate-province resolution, moved by Jonnavittula Gurunatham (ruled out of order); committee under Konda Venkatappayya (secretary) to organise an all-Andhra conference
  [255:0:1.2] Andhra Mahasabha Committee | Guntur, 1912-13 | President Vinjamuri Bhavanacharyulu
  [255:0:1.3] Rayalaseema meeting | Mahanandi, April 1913 | Guthi Kesava Pillai – separation impractical, a "Brahmin movement"
  [255:0:1.4] Vizag district meeting | June 1913 | Manda Suryanarayana (municipal chairman of Vizianagaram); started the weekly Andhra Advocate
[255:0:2] - **First to oppose:** in 1912 **Nyapati Subba Rao** opposed a separate province (too small, would get only a Chief Commissioner); Pattabhi Sitaramayya favoured even a small province.
[255:0:3] - **Growth of opinion 1907-1913:** from Vandemataram (1907) to the first Andhra Conference (1913) – from problems of the people to a province for the people, from district conferences to an Andhra conference.
[255:0:4] # Bapatla, 26-27 May 1913 – the facts
[255:0:5] TABLE head: Particular | Fact
  [255:0:5.0] Date, place | 26-27 May 1913, Bapatla (Guntur district) – not Kakinada, Guntur, Nidadavolu, Madras, Gudivada or Tadepalligudem
  [255:0:5.1] President | B.N. Sarma (Bayya / Baiya Narasimheswara Sarma), member of the Madras Legislative Council – not Nyapati Subba Rao, Pattabhi or Konda Venkatappayya
  [255:0:5.2] Secretary | Konda Venkatappayya
  [255:0:5.3] Attendance | About 800 delegates, 2,000 visitors; delegates also from Hyderabad, Warangal, Nagpur
  [255:0:5.4] Province resolution | Moved by Vemavarapu Ramadasu Pantulu; opposed by Nyapati Subba Rao, M. Adinarayanaiah, Mocherla Ramachandra Rao → amended to "take it up at the next conference" (deferred); a committee under Pattabhi to collect opinion
  [255:0:5.5] University | A separate university for Andhras, with Telugu as medium, first demanded here
  [255:0:5.6] Other agenda | An English daily; lifting the ban on Telugus in the Army; fund for technical training abroad
[255:0:6] - **B.N. Sarma's caution:** the demand was premature and "might do **more harm than good**"; "**First we are Indians, then we are Andhras**" – so he presided but **opposed** a separate state (APPSC G2 2017).
[255:0:7] - **Result:** the awakening got a **respectable forum**; Krishna and Guntur delegates were disappointed; Rayalaseema, Ganjam and Visakhapatnam were lukewarm.
[255:0:8] - After Bapatla, the **Nellore** district meeting called the demand "**not yet ripe**".
[255:0:9] - **Aims of the Andhra movement** (propaganda phase 1913-20): Andhra province, Andhra University, development of Telugu, cultural revival – love of education, culture and high ideals, interest in sanitation, health and physical culture.
[255:0:10] > Trap: President **B.N. Sarma**, secretary **Konda Venkatappayya**, mover **Ramadasu Pantulu**, chief opponent **Nyapati Subba Rao**; the resolution was **passed only at Vijayawada 1914**.
[255:0:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 22 p.4-7; NextGen previous papers p.11; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.17, p.19-20; old app notes 1:255 (sub 1)
## SUB 1 | Andhra Mahasabha Sessions, 1914-1951
[255:1:0] TABLE head: No. | Place, year | President | Fact
  [255:1:0.0] 1st | Bapatla 1913 | B.N. Sarma | University demanded; province deferred
  [255:1:0.1] 2nd | Vijayawada, 11 April 1914 | Nyapati Subba Rao | First called "Andhra Mahasabha"; province resolution passed (moved by Manda Suryanarayana, backed by Ramadasu)
  [255:1:0.2] 3rd | Visakhapatnam, May 1915 | Raja (Panuganti) Rama Rayaningar, Raja of Panagal | Province demand repeated; mother tongue as medium in secondary schools
  [255:1:0.3] 4th | Kakinada, May 1916 | Mocherla Ramachandra Rao ("Gokhale of South India") | Separate Andhra Congress circle; women's session under Achanta Rukmini Lakshmipathi
  [255:1:0.4] 5th | Nellore, 1 June 1917 | Konda Venkatappayya | 480 of 740 delegates from Nellore → district-wise voting (Gadicherla); Madras city demand rejected
  [255:1:0.5] 6th | Kadapa, 1918 | Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao (opposed in 1916, supported in 1918) | Province passed unanimously
[255:1:1] - **Match keys:** 1913 first, 1914 second, 1915 third, 1916 fourth, 1917 fifth (APPSC G2 Mains 2025: 1st B.N. Sarma, 2nd Nyapati, 3rd Rama Rayaningar, 4th Mocherla = a-III, b-II, c-IV, d-I).
[255:1:2] - **1917 and Montagu:** the Mahasabha met at **Vijayawada** (1917 special session) and resolved to put the demand to **Montagu**; delegation led by **Nyapati Subba Rao** met him at Madras on **20 Dec 1917**.
[255:1:3] # Special and later sessions
[255:1:4] TABLE head: Session | President / fact
  [255:1:4.0] Special, Guntur, 17 Aug 1918 | Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao; protested that the Montford proposals gave no Andhra province; Pattabhi proposed an All-India Linguistic States Conference
  [255:1:4.1] Nandyal 1928 | S. Radhakrishnan; on Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's proposal the Ceded districts were renamed Rayalaseema
  [255:1:4.2] Special Andhra Sabha, Madras, 1931 | Kadapa Koti Reddy; resolution given to Gandhi for the 2nd RTC
  [255:1:4.3] Convention, Bellary, 1936 | Vijayananda Gajapati (Vijayanagar); built Coastal-Rayalaseema trust
  [255:1:4.4] Silver Jubilee, Vijayawada, 1937 | Kadapa (K.) Koti Reddy of Cuddapah; Rayalaseema safeguards in cabinet, irrigation, capital
  [255:1:4.5] Madras, 1938 | S. Radhakrishnan (he presided at both Nandyal and Madras)
  [255:1:4.6] Visakhapatnam, Nov 1941; Bellary, 1943 | Sir Vijayananda ("Sir Vijaya"), president 1941-46; met Stafford Cripps, 2 April 1942
  [255:1:4.7] End of 1946 | Sir Vijaya resigned due to ill health → Mahasabha activities stopped
  [255:1:4.8] Guntur, 13-14 Jan 1951 | Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao – the last (25th) session
[255:1:5] - **1921-37:** Gandhian struggles (NCM, no-tax) were followed by Andhra leaders, and **Andhra University (1926)** was won; moderates (Radhakrishnan, C.R. Reddy, Sir Vijaya) kept the Mahasabha going – "Swarajya within Swarajya".
[255:1:6] - **1938:** the **Madras Legislative Assembly passed** (did not reject) a resolution for Andhra and Kerala provinces; on **2 May 1938** Britain said no new provinces would be created.
[255:1:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 22 p.7-9, p.13-14; NextGen AP History Part 23 p.7-8; CDI AP History G2 PYQs 2000-2025 printed p.29-30; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.9, p.14, p.20; old app notes 1:255 (sub 2)
## SUB 2 | The Andhra Congress Circle and the Linguistic Principle
[255:2:0] # Andhras in the Congress
[255:2:1] - **P. Anandacharlu** – **first Telugu President of the INC**, **7th session, Nagpur 1891**; **Pattabhi Sitaramayya** – **Jaipur 1948** (lost **Tripuri 1939** to Bose); **N. Sanjiva Reddy** – 1960-62.
[255:2:2] - **First INC (annual) session in Andhra:** **Kakinada, 1923** – presided by **Maulana Mohammed Ali** (not Pattabhi); the **AICC** met at **Bezawada in 1921** (Tilak Swaraj Fund).
[255:2:3] - **1914 Madras Congress:** **256** Andhra delegates, none on the Working Committee; 1915 Madras provincial conference refused to discuss Andhra; **Lucknow 1916** – examined, no decision.
[255:2:4] # Andhra Congress Circle, 1918
[255:2:5] TABLE head: Particular | Fact
  [255:2:5.0] Sanctioned | Calcutta session, 1917, with Tilak's support
  [255:2:5.1] Formed | 22 January 1918 – the "first victory" of the Andhra movement
  [255:2:5.2] First president | Nyapati Subba Rao (not Kala Venkata Rao, Pattabhi or Konda)
  [255:2:5.3] First secretary | Konda Venkatappayya
[255:2:6] - **Pamphlet "Re-organisation of Indian Provinces":** by **Konda Venkatappayya and Dr. Pattabhi Sitaramayya**, circulated among Congress leaders.
[255:2:7] # Resolutions and the Congress line
[255:2:8] TABLE head: Year | Step
  [255:2:8.0] 1917 | B.N. Sarma moved the separate-province resolution (Madras Council)
  [255:2:8.1] 6 Feb 1918 | B.N. Sarma – linguistic provinces resolution, Imperial Legislative Council; supported by K.V. Rangaswami Ayyangar; opposed by Jinnah and V.S. Srinivasa Sastri; Surendranath Banerjee: "the time has not come"
  [255:2:8.2] July 1918 | Montagu-Chelmsford Report – no Andhra province
  [255:2:8.3] Dec 1920 | Nagpur session (C. Vijayaraghavachariar): Gandhi accepted the linguistic principle; PCCs reorganised on linguistic lines; 4-anna membership, AICC of 350, CWC (no "complete independence by armed means")
  [255:2:8.4] 1922 | M. Suryanarayana (Justice Party) – province resolution in the Madras Council
  [255:2:8.5] 1925, 1926 | Ramadasu Pantulu – amended Dr. Ramarao's resolution for linguistic states (1925); Andhra state proposal in the Council of State (1926, failed)
  [255:2:8.6] 1928 | Nehru Report – linguistic provinces, in line with the 1920 PCC reorganisation
  [255:2:8.7] 1931 | V.V. Jogayya Pantulu to London with the Andhra resolution; Bobbili Raja, Mocherla at the 2nd RTC
  [255:2:8.8] 1938 | Wardha CWC assured the Andhra, Karnataka and Kerala deputation
  [255:2:8.9] 1945-46 | Election manifesto – units on a linguistic and cultural basis
  [255:2:8.10] 1948 | Congress rejected linguistic provinces for the time being (Dhar, JVP)
[255:2:9] - **Raja of Bobbili** (Justice Party), Chief Minister of Madras from **1932**, **opposed** Andhra separation.
[255:2:10] - **Regionalism:** the demand for **states on a linguistic basis** was one of the first manifestations of regionalism in India.

[255:2:12] - **1922:** Jayanti Ramayya Pantulu said the Madras Presidency, with its diverse elements, was unsuitable as an administrative unit (printed key).
## SUB 3 | Causes, Press and Early Writings
[255:3:0] # Grievances in the Madras Presidency
[255:3:1] - Telugus about **40%** of the Presidency's people (58% of its area), lumped as "Madrasis"; dominant language **Tamil**; Tamils taunted them for lacking figures like Bhasyam Aiyengar.
[255:3:2] TABLE head: Post (c. 1911) | Telugu | Non-Telugu
  [255:3:2.0] High posts (64) | 8 | 56
  [255:3:2.1] Deputy Collectors | 21 | 39
  [255:3:2.2] District Munsifs | 30 | 93
  [255:3:2.3] District Judges | 0 | 19
[255:3:3] - **Main cause:** **unequal opportunities in education, employment and administration**; higher, technical and professional education out of reach (1915: 8 of 31 colleges, **no engineering, medical or law college**); Anglo-Indian officers knowing little Telugu.
[255:3:4] - Revenue grievance: surplus of the Andhra **deltas** spent on Tamil areas; early demands – province, university, **port at Visakhapatnam**.
[255:3:5] - **Keenest:** **Krishna and Guntur**; lukewarm: Rayalaseema, Nellore, Ganjam, Visakhapatnam.
[255:3:6] - **Precedent:** Bengal partition 1905, annulled 1911; **Bihar** separation announced at the **Delhi Durbar, 12 Dec 1911** → Bihar and Orissa province 1 April 1912 → provinces could be redrawn on linguistic lines.
[255:3:7] - **Tamil press:** opposed and **raised doubts about the Andhras' ability** to run a province; an Andhra Patrika writer replied that separation would **not harm national unity**.
[255:3:8] # Writings and papers
[255:3:9] TABLE head: Paper / writing | Person | Fact
  [255:3:9.0] Andhrula Charitra (1910, Vignana Chandrika Mandali) | Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao | History of the Andhras – inspired pride
  [255:3:9.1] "On the present position of the Telugu people" ("Telugu Prajala Prasthuta Paristhiti") | Jonnavittula Gurunatham (Gurunadham) of Guntur | Six articles in The Hindu, 1911 – began the Andhrodyamam
  [255:3:9.2] Deshabhimani (Guntur) | Anglo-Telugu paper, only daily of British Andhra | 19 Jan 1910 call for Andhra unity; 4 Feb 1910 call for a political meeting; "no protection for Telugu culture without its own government"
  [255:3:9.3] Krishna Patrika | Konda Venkatappayya, 1 Feb 1902; editor Mutnuri Krishna Rao | Voice of the Telugu districts
  [255:3:9.4] Andhra Patrika | Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao, Bombay 1908, later Madras | Popularised the word "Andhra"
  [255:3:9.5] Andhra Kesari (1904, Rajahmundry) | Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao | –
  [255:3:9.6] Desamata (Rajahmundry) | Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham | –
  [255:3:9.7] Swarajya (Vijayawada) | Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao | –
  [255:3:9.8] Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae | T. Prakasam | Madras an Andhra city
[255:3:10] - **Guntur group:** Jonnavittula Gurunadham with Challa Seshagiri Rao, Gollapudi Seeta Rama Sastri, Unnava Lakshminarayana, Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya; **Bandar (1908)** non-political conference under **Gurunadham** (printed key).
[255:3:11] > Trap: the Hindu articles are **Gurunatham's**, not Sitarama Sastri's (an APPSC G2 2017 key).
[255:3:12] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 22 p.4-5; NextGen previous papers p.11; NextGen AP History Part 16 p.11; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.18; old app notes 1:255 (sub 0)
[255:3:13] - **Colleges (1913):** of **31** colleges in the Presidency, Andhra had **3 first-grade and 5 second-grade** (8 in all).
## SUB 4 | Sri Bagh Pact, 1937
[255:4:0] TABLE head: Particular | Fact
  [255:4:0.0] Date | 16 November 1937

  [255:4:2.0] University | Two centres of Andhra University – Waltair and Anantapur

  [255:4:2.2] Legislature | General seats shared on an equal district-wise basis
  [255:4:2.3] Capital / High Court | In different regions – Rayalaseema chooses first
[255:4:3] - **Implemented 1953:** capital **Kurnool**, High Court **Guntur**; it served as a model for the **Gentlemen's Agreement (1956, 60:40 cabinet)**; still cited in Rayalaseema capital, High Court and irrigation debates.

## SUB 7 | After 1947 – Dhar, JVP and the Madras Question
[255:7:0] - **Nov 1947:** Nehru backed Andhra; dropped from the **Draft Constitution (21 Feb 1948)**; Centre feared for **national unity**; Nehru promised a committee on his **1948 Visakhapatnam** visit.
[255:7:1] TABLE head: Body | Appointed by / date | Members | Finding
  [255:7:1.0] Dhar Commission (Linguistic Provinces Commission) | President of the Constituent Assembly, 17 June 1948 | Justice S.K. Dhar; Dr. Panna Lal, Jagat Narayan Lal | Report 10 Dec 1948: administrative convenience, not language; linguistic states a threat to national unity; mandate – Andhra, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra
  [255:7:1.1] JVP Committee | Congress, Jaipur session, Dec 1948 | Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya – not N. Sanjiva Reddy | Report April 1949: postpone; Andhra if the claim to Madras is dropped; reaffirmed Dhar; "if public opinion is insistent and overwhelming, we as democrats have to submit"
  [255:7:1.2] Partition Committee | Madras govt, Dec 1949 | Chair P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja; Andhra: Prakasam, Kala Venkatrao, Bezawada Gopala Reddy, N. Sanjiva Reddy | Assets and liabilities; report 4 Jan 1950; Prakasam's separate note
  [255:7:1.3] Wanchoo inquiry | Centre, Dec 1952 | Justice K.N. Wanchoo | Financial and administrative implications of Andhra State
[255:7:2] - **CWC:** Andhra **without Madras city**; Andhra Mahasabha wanted the state by **26 Jan 1950**; Visalandhra Mahasabha (1949) – all Telugu areas.
[255:7:3] TABLE head: Person | Stand on Madras
  [255:7:3.0] Raja of Panagal | Cooum river boundary
  [255:7:3.1] Andhra Congress | Half of Madras town
  [255:7:3.2] Rajaji, later Kamaraj | No sharing; Rajaji left Rayalaseema out of his 1937 cabinet
[255:7:4] - **"Andhra exception"** opened the way to the **SRC** and nationwide linguistic reorganisation; splits (Circars vs Rayalaseema, **Prakasam vs Pattabhi**) slowed the movement.

[255:7:7] - **Prakasam, Madras CM 1946-47:** after the **April 1946** elections **T. Prakasam** became Chief Minister of Madras (Rajaji led the 1937 ministry).
## SUB 8 | The Fasts – Swami Sitaram and Potti Sriramulu
[255:8:0] # Swami Sitaram, 1951
[255:8:1] - **Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri**; fast at **Guntur, 15 Aug - 20 Sept 1951, 35 days**; demands – Andhra by **2 Oct 1951**, Madras city's status settled in three years (no Telangana merger demand).
[255:8:2] - Ended on **Vinoba Bhave's** appeal, no gain. April 1951 APCC poll: **Sanjiva Reddy beat N.G. Ranga by 5 votes** → Prakasam and Ranga formed the **Kisan Mazdoor Praja Party**.
[255:8:3] # Potti Sriramulu
[255:8:4] - Born **16 March 1901, Madras**; **Arya Vysya**; ancestral village **Gajula Dinne, Nellore**; about **3 years at Sabarmati**; khadi, prohibition, **Harijan uplift**.

  [255:8:5.2] 1949 | Gandhi Smarak Din
[255:8:6] # The death fast, 1952
[255:8:7] TABLE head: Event | Date

  [255:8:7.1] Death | 15 Dec 1952, 58th day → "Amarajeevi"
  [255:8:7.2] Nehru's announcement | 19 Dec 1952 – Andhra from the undisputed Telugu areas, excluding Madras city
[255:8:8] - **Aims:** immediate announcement; unity of Andhra leaders; Madras a Chief Commissioner's State – for the Telugu districts of **Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema**.
[255:8:9] - Aftermath: riots, police firing – **seven** died.
[255:8:10] - **Memory:** **Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District (2008)**; Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University; **58-ft "Statue of Sacrifice"**, Amaravati, unveiled **16 Mar 2026** (125th birth anniversary).

=== NOTES 1:256 | Wanchoo Committee and the Problems of the New Andhra State
## SUB 0 | Capital, High Court and the Bellary Taluks
[256:0:0] # Capital of Andhra State (1953)
[256:0:1] - **Capital:** **Kurnool** – temporary capital of Andhra State from its formation on **1 October 1953** (APPSC JA 2023: "Kurnool became the capital in **1953**").
[256:0:2] - **How it was chosen:** Rayalaseema legislators wanted the capital in their region as promised by the **Sribagh Pact**; the communists favoured **Vijayawada**; in the vote of the legislators **Kurnool won by majority**, but only with the help of **five non-Andhra members** of the residual Madras Assembly (C. Rajagopalachari had suggested they should not vote).
[256:0:3]   - Counted without the five non-Andhra votes, Vijayawada-Guntur would have had the edge – hence some keys answer "None" to "capital chosen with the support of the majority".
[256:0:4] - **Nehru's condition (25 Mar 1953):** capital to be **inside Andhra**, not Madras; temporary capital to be decided **before 1 July 1953**; some offices could stay in Madras for a while.
[256:0:5] # High Court
[256:0:6] - **Andhra High Court:** set up at **Guntur** in **1954** (first Chief Justice **Koka Subba Rao**) – the compromise for coastal Andhra, while the capital went to Kurnool; not Kurnool, Vijayawada or Anantapur.
[256:0:7] - **Interim:** the **Madras High Court** kept jurisdiction until the Guntur court was set up.
[256:0:8] # Bellary district split
[256:0:9] TABLE head: Bellary area | Went to
  [256:0:9.0] Alur (Aalur), Adoni | Andhra – Kurnool district
  [256:0:9.1] Rayadurg | Andhra – Anantapur district
  [256:0:9.2] Bellary taluk, Siruguppa, Hospet, Sandur, Harpanahalli, Hadagali | Mysore
[256:0:10] - **Justice L.S. Mishra** (Chief Justice, **Hyderabad High Court**): Bellary inquiry (hearings 1-15 May 1953); on his report **Bellary taluk went to Mysore**.
[256:0:11] - **Legislature:** members elected to the **Madras Assembly in 1952** formed the Andhra Assembly; **unicameral – no Legislative Council**.
[256:0:12] > Exam angle: Kurnool capital / Guntur High Court (×4); Alur-Adoni → Kurnool, Rayadurg → Anantapur.
[256:0:13] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 19 p.20; NextGen AP History Part 23 p.15; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.7, p.9; Wikipedia "Andhra State Act, 1953" (Bellary taluks, High Court at Guntur); app notes 1:256 (sub 3, 5)
## SUB 1 | Wanchoo Committee and the Andhra State Act, 1953
[256:1:0] # Wanchoo Committee
[256:1:1] TABLE head: Particular | Fact
  [256:1:1.0] Appointed | December 1952, after Nehru's statement of 19 December 1952 (following Potti Sriramulu's death)
  [256:1:1.1] Member | Justice Kailas Nath (K.N.) Wanchoo, Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court – a single-member committee
  [256:1:1.2] Task | To report on the financial and other implications of forming Andhra State – identifying the problems of forming the state (boundaries, finances, division of assets, administration); not the capital of India, not the Nizam or peasants
  [256:1:1.3] Report | 7 February 1953
  [256:1:1.4] Centre's decisions on it | Announced by Nehru on 25 March 1953
[256:1:2] - **NextGen's dates differ:** NextGen gives "appointed 7 Feb 1953, report 25 Mar 1953"; the Lok Sabha record has the report presented on 7 Feb 1953 and the decisions announced on 25 Mar 1953.
[256:1:3] - **On Madras:** Wanchoo suggested the Andhra Government work temporarily from **Madras** (not Kurnool) for **3-5 years**; Nehru rejected it – "no question" of Madras as capital.
[256:1:4] - **Earlier:** **Partition Committee (1949-50)** under **Kumaraswamy Raja** on asset split; **JVP Committee (April 1949)** – Andhra only if Telugus gave up Madras.
[256:1:5] - **Special Officer:** **C.M. Trivedi**, later the first Governor.
[256:1:6] # Finances, assets and services
[256:1:7] - Assets and administration divided between Andhra and **residual Madras**; the Wanchoo apportionment of **assets and liabilities** was largely reproduced in the Act's schedule.
[256:1:8] - The 25 Mar 1953 statement left **services** and **financial implications** to be considered separately later.
[256:1:9] - New state "**administratively and economically orphaned**": no developed capital, no commercial centre.
[256:1:10] # Andhra State Act, 1953
[256:1:11] - **Act 30 of 1953**; **assent of the President: 14 September 1953**; in force **1 October 1953** – not May or June 1953.
[256:1:12] - **2014 parallels:** **Kamalanathan** committee – employees; **Sheela Bhide** committee – Schedule IX institutions; **Section 6** expert committee – new capital.
[256:1:13] > Exam angle: Wanchoo = financial and other implications (×2); Bill assent 14 Sept 1953.
[256:1:14] ~~ Sources: web search snippets of the Lok Sabha statement of 25 Mar 1953 (eparlib.nic.in; page not opened); Wikipedia "Andhra State" and "Andhra State Act, 1953" (assent 14 Sept 1953); NextGen AP History Part 19 p.20; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.12; app notes 1:256 (sub 0-4)
## SUB 2 | Tungabhadra Project and the Sribagh Pact
[256:2:0] TABLE head: Pact / Act | Year | Provision
  [256:2:0.0] Sribagh (Sreebagh) Pact | 1937 | Irrigation priority for Rayalaseema and Nellore on the Krishna, Penna and Tungabhadra – for 10 years or as long as needed
  [256:2:0.1] Andhra State Act | 1953 | Tungabhadra Board constituted by the President under Section 66(4) of this Act to manage the works – not the River Boards Act 1956 or the AP Reorganisation Act 2014
[256:2:1] - After Bellary's division the Tungabhadra works were shared by **Andhra and Mysore**.
[256:2:2] - **26 Jun 2026:** Union Minister **C.R. Patil** opened **33 new gates** of the Tungabhadra dam with the three CMs.
[256:2:3] > Exam angle: Sribagh rivers = Krishna, Penna, Tungabhadra (not Godavari or Musi).
[256:2:4] ~~ Sources: app notes 1:256 (sub 6); general knowledge, not checked (Section 66(4))

=== NOTES 1:257 | Role of the Press and Newspapers in the Andhra Movement
## SUB 0 | First Telugu Papers – Satyadoota and Other Firsts
[257:0:0] # Satyadoota (Satya Duta) – the first Telugu journal
[257:0:1] - **Satyadoota:** the **first Telugu newspaper / journal / magazine**, started in **1835** at **Bellary** by the **Christian missionaries (Bellary Christian Society / Association)** to **propagate Christianity** – not Vruttanthini, Vartamana Tarangini, Desabhimani, Tattvabodhini or Andhra Patrika.
[257:0:2] - **Tattvabodhini (1864, Madras):** published by the **Madras Veda Samaj** for the propagation of Hinduism; supported widow remarriage.
[257:0:3] # Other "firsts" and "only"
[257:0:4] TABLE head: First / only | Paper
  [257:0:4.0] First Telugu newspaper printed in Andhra | Hitavadi (1841), Edmund Park
  [257:0:4.1] First Telugu paper started by a Muslim | Vartamana Tarangini (8 June 1842, Madras) – Syed Rahamatullah; passed to Puvvada Seshagiri Rao after 1843
  [257:0:4.2] First political weekly / journal in Telugu | Andhra Prakasika (1885) – A.P. Parthasarathi Naidu
  [257:0:4.3] Only Telugu daily of British Andhra | Desabhimani (Guntur)
  [257:0:4.4] First fully socialist Telugu journal | Navasakthi
  [257:0:4.5] First communist Telugu journal | Prajasakthi
  [257:0:4.6] First Telugu journal after independence | Jaya Bharat
  [257:0:4.7] Introduced the editorial column | Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani – Kokkonda Venkataratnam
  [257:0:4.8] First newspaper from Madras | Madras Courier (1785) – not The Hindu or The Mail
[257:0:5] - **Purushartha Pradayini (1872, Machilipatnam):** articles for and against widow remarriage.
[257:0:6] - **By 1905:** about **20** Telugu journals – Andhra Prakasika, Sasilekha, Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani, Rasikollasini.
[257:0:7] > Exam angle: Satyadoota–Bellary–1835–missionaries (×9, the most repeated fact of the topic); Andhra Prakasika = first political weekly.
[257:0:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 18 p.3-4; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.11, p.14, p.19; NextGen AP History Part 20 p.1-2; app notes 1:257 (sub 0, 1); general knowledge, not checked (Madras Courier 1785)
## SUB 1 | Papers and Their Founders / Editors
[257:1:0] TABLE head: Paper | Year / place | Founder / editor
  [257:1:0.0] Andhra Prakasika | 1885 | A.P. Parthasarathi Naidu – not P. Anandacharlu (the classic wrong match), N. Subba Rao or Mutnuri
  [257:1:0.1] Krishna Patrika | 1902, Machilipatnam | Konda Venkatappayya (and Dasu Narayana Rao)
  [257:1:0.2] Andhra Patrika | 9 Sept 1908, Bombay → Madras | Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao – founder and first editor; daily from 1914
  [257:1:0.3] The Crescent | Madras (English) | Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty
  [257:1:0.4] Swarajya (Telugu) | 1907, Vijayawada | Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao – earlier *Sri Venkateswara Patrika*
  [257:1:0.5] Swarajya (English daily) | 26 Oct 1921, Madras | Tanguturi Prakasam – to spread the Congress message
  [257:1:0.6] Desabhimani | Guntur | Devaguptam Seshachalapati Rao – earlier *Krishnavrittantini*
  [257:1:0.7] Zamin Ryot | 1930, Nellore (weekly) | Nellore Venkatarama Naidu – peasant, anti-zamindari issues
  [257:1:0.8] Andhra Prabha | 15 Aug 1938, Madras | Indian Express group (Ramnath Goenka); noted editor Narla Venkateswara Rao (not Kasinathuni); started to challenge Andhra Patrika
  [257:1:0.9] Golconda Patrika | 1926 | Suravaram Pratapa Reddy
  [257:1:0.10] Manorama (1906), Desamata (1910) | Rajahmundry | Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham
  [257:1:0.11] Manoranjani | 1910 | Kallakuri Narayana Rao
  [257:1:0.12] Andhra Sahitya Parishad Patrika | – | Jayanti Ramayya Pantulu
  [257:1:0.13] Andhra Bhasa Sanjivani | – | Kokkonda Venkataratnam
  [257:1:0.14] Andhra Kesari | Rajahmundry | Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao
  [257:1:0.15] Deccan Chronicle | 1938, Hyderabad | Rajagopal Mudaliar
[257:1:1] - **Match (APPSC JA 2023):** Andhra Patrika–Kasinathuni, Krishna Patrika–Konda Venkatappayya, Andhra Prakasika–Parthasarathi Naidu, The Crescent–Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty.
[257:1:2] - **Two Swarajyas:** Gadicherla's Telugu Swarajya (1907) vs Prakasam's English daily (1921); a question on the "English daily Swarajya" = **Prakasam**.
[257:1:3] - **Gadicherla and Andhra Patrika:** edited Andhra Patrika in 1916-18 (app notes).
[257:1:4] - **Malathi Chandur:** ran the women's feature **"Pramadavanam"** in the **Andhra Prabha weekly** from the 1950s.
[257:1:5] - **Women's papers:** Hindu Sundari (1902; Mosalikanti Ramabayamma, Vempati Santabayamma), Sri Savitri (1904; Pulaguri Laxminarasamamba).
[257:1:6] - **Gurajada Appa Rao:** attempted *Prakasika* (1896).
[257:1:7] > Exam angle: Andhra Prakasika–Parthasarathi Naidu (×4, incl. the Anandacharlu wrong match); English Swarajya–Prakasam (×2).
[257:1:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 7 p.9, p.11, p.28; NextGen AP History Part 18 p.4; NextGen AP History Part 20 p.1-2; app notes 1:257 (sub 2, 4, 7); general knowledge, not checked (The Crescent, Deccan Chronicle, Pramadavanam)
## SUB 2 | Press and the Separate-Andhra Demand
[257:2:0] - **April 1911 – The Hindu:** a series of **six articles** by **Jonnavittula Gurunatham** (Guntur), "on the present position (condition) of the Telugu people", showed the under-representation of Telugus – not Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani or Indian Patriot.
[257:2:1]   - "Are Telugu people backward?" (15 Apr 1911): civil services **56 non-Andhras : 8 Andhras**; district judges **19 : 0**.
[257:2:2] - **Desabhimani (1911):** urged a separate Andhra political conference and Telugu papers writing on Andhra affairs; commented "**Unless there is a separate Government there is no protection for Telugu people's culture**".
[257:2:3] - **Krishna Patrika:** printed several articles on the need for a **separate Andhra province** (1912 debate with Desamata); 30 Nov 1912 – "strengthening the nation begins with the Andhra movement"; 19 Jul 1913 cartoon – Rayalaseema as an iceberg blocking the "Andhra Movement" ship.
[257:2:4] - **Janmabhumi (25 Aug 1920):** the Andhra movement strengthens national unity.
[257:2:5] - **Supporters of a separate Andhra:** Andhra Patrika, Krishna Patrika, Desabhimani, Desamata, Darbar; Andhra Patrika popularised the word "Andhra".
[257:2:6] - **Significance:** the press spread the national movement and built support for the separate-Andhra demand; newspapers also gave rise to reading rooms and libraries.
[257:2:7] > Exam angle: 1911 six articles = The Hindu; Desabhimani's "separate Government" remark.
[257:2:8] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 22 p.4-5; NextGen AP History Part 6 p.12; app notes 1:257 (sub 7, 8)
## SUB 3 | Veeresalingam's Journals
[257:3:0] TABLE head: Journal | Year
  [257:3:0.0] Vivekavardhani | 1874 – his first journal, to carry social reform
  [257:3:0.1] Hasyasanjivani | 1876
  [257:3:0.2] Sati Hitabodhini | 1883
  [257:3:0.3] Satyasamvardhini | 1891
  [257:3:0.4] Zenana Patrika | 1894 (women's education)
  [257:3:0.5] Satyavadini | 1905
[257:3:1] - **Own press:** 1876.
[257:3:2] - **Chintamani:** jointly edited by Veeresalingam and **Nyapati Subba Rao**.
[257:3:3] - **Counter-journals:** Hasyavardhani (Kokkonda Venkataratnam) against Vivekavardhani; NextGen also credits a *Satyasamvardhini* and the *Telugu Zenana* to **Rayasam Venkata Sivudu**.
[257:3:4] > Exam angle: 1874 = Vivekavardhani; "Hitabodhini", "Zanana", "Sanjivani" are inexact names – the exact one offered is Satyasamvardhini.
[257:3:5] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 20 p.1; NextGen AP History Part 6 p.12; NextGen AP History Part 18 p.4; app notes 1:257 (sub 4)
## SUB 4 | Press Against the Government – Grievances and Movements
[257:4:0] - **Lokaranjani (October 1875):** complained that the ryots were **better off under the East India Company** than under the Crown.
[257:4:1] - **Home Rule:** **Desamata (Desha Mata)** – Chilakamarti's Rajahmundry paper – strongly supported the **Home Rule movement** in Andhra (APPSC G2 Mains 2017) – not Andhra Mata; **Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao** was the Andhra Home Rule leader (secretary).
[257:4:2] TABLE head: Movement | Paper
  [257:4:2.0] Vandemataram / Swadeshi | Krishna Patrika, Swarajya, Desamata, Andhra Kesari (Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao), Navayuga
  [257:4:2.1] Home Rule | Desamata
  [257:4:2.2] Peasant / anti-zamindari | Zamin Ryot
  [257:4:2.3] Socialist / Communist | Navasakthi / Prajasakthi
  [257:4:2.4] Women's cause | Hindu Sundari (1902), Sri Savitri (1904)
[257:4:3] - **Vernacular Press Act, 1878** ("Gagging Act") – repealed by **Lord Ripon, 1882**.
[257:4:4] - **Swarajya sedition case:** Gadicherla (with Bodi Narayana Rao) convicted under **Section 124A IPC** for an article of 26 March 1908; **3 years** – the first Telugu editor in the Presidency imprisoned in the Vandemataram movement.
[257:4:5] - **"Veerabali":** NextGen says **Krowidi Lingaraju** was jailed for two years for the editorial "Veerabali" (1920s); Madduri Annapurnayya for the playlet "Chichula Pidugu".
[257:4:6] > Exam angle: Home Rule paper = Desamata; Lokaranjani 1875.
[257:4:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 6 p.3, p.12; NextGen AP History Part 20 p.2; NextGen AP History Part 18 p.26; app notes 1:257 (sub 5, 6)

=== NOTES 1:261 | States Reorganisation Commission (fazl Ali) and the States Reorganisation Act 1956
## SUB 0 | Andhra State 1953 – the First Linguistic State
[261:0:0] - **First linguistic state of independent India:** **Andhra State**, formed **1 October 1953**, the forerunner of **Andhra Pradesh** (exam keys write "Andhra Pradesh") – not Orissa, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan or Karnataka.
[261:0:1] - **Carved out of:** **Madras State** (Rayalaseema + Coastal Andhra; Madras city excluded) – not Hyderabad, Mysore or Bombay State.
[261:0:2] - **Date trap:** **1 October 1953** – not "April 1953" or 1956. **1 Nov 1956** is the birth of **Andhra Pradesh** (Andhra State + Telangana).
[261:0:3] - **Capital:** **Kurnool** (1953–56), chosen over Vijayawada by **80 to 79** in the Assembly (with five non-Andhra votes) – not Hyderabad, Madras, Kadapa, Nellore, Amaravati or Visakhapatnam. **Hyderabad** became capital only of Andhra Pradesh (1956).
[261:0:4] - **Potti Sriramulu:** fasted in **Madras** (Bulusu Sambamurthy's house) from **19 Oct 1952**; died **15 Dec 1952** after **58 days** (Laxmikanth: 56-day fast) → unrest → Nehru announced Andhra State on **19 Dec 1952**.
[261:0:5] TABLE head: Item | Andhra State | Andhra Pradesh
  [261:0:5.0] Formed | 1 Oct 1953 | 1 Nov 1956
  [261:0:5.1] Capital | Kurnool | Hyderabad
  [261:0:5.2] First CM | Tanguturi Prakasam | N. Sanjiva Reddy
  [261:0:5.3] Basis | Andhra State Act after Sriramulu's death | SR Act 1956 (after SRC)
[261:0:6] > Exam angle: "first linguistic state" → Andhra (1953, from Madras, capital Kurnool); "Andhra Pradesh formed after the SRC" → 1956.
[261:0:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 19 p.20; Part 20 p.7; Part 23 p.15-16; Part 6 p.4; Part 8 p.27; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Part 1 p.97, p.101; app notes 1:261 (sub 2)
## SUB 1 | SRC – Appointment, Chairman and Members
[261:1:0] - **Trigger:** creation of **Andhra State (1953)** set off similar demands elsewhere.
[261:1:1] - **Announced 22 December 1953** by PM **Nehru** in Parliament (APPSC G2 2017) – not 20, 21 or 23 December.
[261:1:2] - **Constituted** by Home Ministry Resolution No. 53/69/53-Public of **29 December 1953**. Year of appointment = **1953** (not 1949, 1955 or 1956).
[261:1:3] TABLE head: Member | Position
  [261:1:3.0] Syed (Saiyid) Fazl Ali | Chairman – then Governor of Odisha
  [261:1:3.1] H.N. Kunzru | Member
  [261:1:3.2] K.M. Panikkar | Member
[261:1:4] - **NOT members:** **Tej Bahadur Sapru**, K.N. Wanchoo, Pattabhi Sitaramayya, Vallabhbhai Patel, Nehru, C.M. Trivedi (first Governor of AP), K. Brahmananda Reddy, D. Sanjivaiah, Rajaji.
[261:1:5] > Exam angle: SRC = **Fazl Ali + Kunzru + Panikkar**, announced **22 Dec 1953**, report **30 Sep 1955**.
[261:1:6] ~~ Sources: SRC Report 1955, Introduction para 1 (archive.org dli.csl.689); NextGen AP History Part 19 p.20; Part 20 p.3; Part 6 p.13; Part 7 p.24; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Part 1 p.98
## SUB 2 | SR Act 1956 and the Formation of Andhra Pradesh
[261:2:0] - **Key dates:** SRC report (in **four parts**) **30 Sep 1955** → **Gentlemen's Agreement 20 Feb 1956** → **SR Act (Act 37 of 1956) enacted 31 August 1956** → in force, **Andhra Pradesh formed 1 November 1956**.
[261:2:1] - **Andhra Pradesh = Andhra State + Telugu districts of Hyderabad (Telangana)**, formed under **Section 3** of the Act – the **first state formed under the SR Act** (not Mysore); first CM **N. Sanjiva Reddy**, first Governor **C.M. Trivedi**. Date of AP's formation = **1956** (not 1953).
[261:2:2] - **Result:** **14 states + 6 Union Territories** from 1 Nov 1956 (SR Act + 7th Amendment); also bilingual Bombay, enlarged Madras, new Mysore, Kerala. **APPSC** was set up in **1956**.
[261:2:3] # Andhra–Telangana politics, 1955-56
[261:2:4] - **Andhra:** CM **Bezawada Gopala Reddy's** resolution (Telangana priority, population-based shares) passed **unanimously** (1955). **Communists** consistently backed integrated linguistic states and **Visalandhra**.
[261:2:5] - **Hyderabad Assembly vote** (174 members): **103 for** Visalandhra, **29 against**, **15 neutral**; CM **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** worked to allay Telangana's fears on the High Command's direction.
[261:2:6] - **22 Oct 1955:** the two CMs agreed to merge at **Hyderabad House, New Delhi**. **Nov 1955:** Congress sub-committee **Nehru, G.B. Pant, Maulana Azad** (Azad kept opposing).
[261:2:7] - **Gentlemen's Agreement (20 Feb 1956, Hyderabad House):** **Telangana Regional Council**, Telangana surplus spent in Telangana, **Mulki rules** retained. The Centre thus **overrode the SRC's wait-till-1961 formula** by political agreement.
[261:2:8] - **Nehru (1956):** the merger a "**matrimonial alliance**" with a provision for **divorce** – later cited by separate-Telangana advocates.
[261:2:9] > Exam angle: 31 Aug 1956 (enacted) vs 1 Nov 1956 (in force); 14 + 6.
[261:2:10] ~~ Sources: States Reorganisation Act 1956 text, p.6 (thc.nic.in); SRC Report 1955 contents (archive.org dli.csl.689); NextGen AP History Part 16 p.13; Part 23 p.22, p.24; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Part 1 p.98; app notes 1:261 (sub 6, 7)
## SUB 3 | SRC Report 1955 – Principles and Hyderabad/Visalandhra
[261:3:0] - **Report:** submitted **30 Sep 1955**, made public **9 Oct 1955**; **1,52,250** memorandums; **four parts** – I Conditions of the Problem, II Factors Bearing on Reorganisation, III Proposals for Reorganisation, IV Administrative and Allied Matters (safeguards for linguistic groups).
[261:3:1] - **Principles:** language **important but not the only factor**; rejected "**one language, one state**" – same-language areas could form more than one state; other factors: **unity and security of India**, **administrative efficiency**, **financial and economic viability**, national plans.
[261:3:2] - **Recommended 16 states + 3 centrally administered territories**; abolish the **Part A/B/C** classification.
[261:3:3] TABLE head: Region | SRC recommendation
  [261:3:3.0] Vidarbha | Separate state
  [261:3:3.1] Bombay | Bilingual (Gujarati + Marathi)
  [261:3:3.2] Punjabi Suba | Not accepted
  [261:3:3.3] Telugu districts of Hyderabad | Separate Hyderabad State (para 386)
[261:3:4] # Hyderabad (Part III ch. V) and Andhra (ch. VI)
[261:3:5] - **Division of Hyderabad State:** most regions (Telugu, Kannada, Marathi) wanted it divided; **Kannada areas (Raichur, Gulbarga) → Mysore**; **Marathwada → Bombay** State.
[261:3:6] - **Para 368:** 45.4% Urdu speakers in Hyderabad–Secunderabad, but **no Union Territory** for the twin cities.
[261:3:7] - **Para 371 (for Visalandhra):** a state of ~32 million with water, power and minerals; "the **twin cities of Hyderabad and Secunderabad** are very well suited to be the capital of Vishalandhra" – this would **solve Andhra's permanent-capital problem** (not Kurnool).
[261:3:8] - **Para 386:** Telangana to function initially as **Hyderabad State**; merger **after the 1961 elections** if **two-thirds** of elected Telangana legislators agree.
[261:3:9] TABLE head: For Visalandhra (paras 369–374) | Against immediate merger
  [261:3:9.0] Large state, rich in minerals, water, power | Advanced Coastal Andhra would dominate services
  [261:3:9.1] Hyderabad solves Andhra's capital problem | Mulki rules and local jobs at risk
  [261:3:9.2] Unified Krishna–Godavari development | Telangana's revenue surplus diverted
[261:3:10] - **Reactions:** **Tenneti Viswanatham** called the report **self-contradictory**; the departure from para 386 became the core grievance of the Telangana movements (**1969, 2001–14**).
[261:3:11] > Exam angle: twin-city capital = **Hyderabad and Secunderabad**; "Kurnool as capital solves the problem" = wrong.
[261:3:12] ~~ Sources: SRC Report 1955, contents and paras 368-386 (archive.org dli.csl.689); NextGen AP History Part 23 p.20-21; Part 20 p.3-4; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Part 1 p.98; app notes 1:261 (sub 4, 5)
## SUB 4 | Bodies Before the SRC – Dhar, JVP, Partition Committees, Wanchoo
[261:4:0] TABLE head: Body | Year | Members / view
  [261:4:0.0] S.K. Dhar Commission (Linguistic Provinces Commission) | appointed 17 June 1948; report Dec 1948 | Linguistic states a threat to national unity; preferred administrative convenience
  [261:4:0.1] JVP Committee | Dec 1948 – Apr 1949 | Nehru, Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya; rejected language as the immediate basis; advised postponement
  [261:4:0.2] Partition Committee (Madras) | 1949–50 | Chaired by Madras CM P.S. Kumaraswami Raja
  [261:4:0.3] Partition Committee (Madras) | 1953 | Appointed by CM C. Rajagopalachari; members of his Cabinet only
  [261:4:0.4] Wanchoo inquiry | 1953 | Justice K.N. Wanchoo (CJ, Rajasthan HC); financial and administrative issues of separating Andhra
[261:4:1] - **1948 report calling linguistic states a threat to unity:** the **Dhar Commission** – not the JVP Report (1949), Krishnamachari or Wanchoo.
[261:4:2] > Exam angle: Dhar = administrative convenience (1948); JVP = postpone (1949).
[261:4:3] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 23 p.10-11; Laxmikanth 8th ed. Part 1 p.97; NextGen Polity APPSC 13 p.11; app notes 1:261 (sub 1)
## SUB 5 | Linguistic States – Arguments and Background
[261:5:0] - **For** linguistic states: government and administration in the **people's language** – **administration becomes easier**; cultural identity. **Against**: fear for unity after Partition, regionalism, border and minority disputes (e.g. **Belgaum**, Maharashtra–Karnataka).
[261:5:1] TABLE head: Year | Milestone
  [261:5:1.0] 1918 | B.N. Sharma moved the linguistic reorganisation resolution in the Imperial Legislative Council
  [261:5:1.1] 1928 | Tanguturi Prakasam – "Andhra Kesari", bared his chest to police guns in the Simon Commission boycott, Madras
  [261:5:1.2] 1930 | First Nizam Andhra Mahasabha, Jogipet (Suravaram Pratapa Reddy)
  [261:5:1.3] 1936 | Orissa = first province on linguistic lines
  [261:5:1.4] 1937 | Visalandhra idea starts in the Circar districts; Sri Bagh Pact (16 Nov) – irrigation priority, university centres, equal legislative seats for Rayalaseema (no Telangana merger)
  [261:5:1.5] 1949 | Visalandhra Mahasabha formed (Nov 1949, Vijayawada)
[261:5:2] ~~ Sources: NextGen AP History Part 20 p.3; Part 23 p.17; app notes 1:261 (sub 0, 2, 9)
## SUB 6 | Seventh Amendment 1956, Zonal Councils and Later Changes
[261:6:0] - **7th Constitutional Amendment (1956):** abolished **Part A/B/C/D** → **14 states and 6 UTs**; abolished the **Rajpramukh**; **extended the jurisdiction of High Courts to Union Territories** and allowed a common High Court for two or more states (not the 1st, 3rd or 5th Amendment); inserted **Art 350A** (mother-tongue instruction at primary stage) and **Art 350B** (Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities).
[261:6:1] # Zonal Councils (SR Act Part III, Sections 15–22)
[261:6:2] - **Five** statutory councils – Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, Southern; purpose **inter-state cooperation**.
[261:6:3] - **Chairman:** a Union Minister nominated by the President – in practice the **Union Home Minister**; Vice-Chairman: a member-state CM by annual rotation. Members: **CM + two ministers** of each state; up to two from each UT.
[261:6:4] - **APRA 2014** amended **Section 15** of the SR Act to read "Andhra Pradesh and Telangana".
[261:6:5] # Later changes
[261:6:6] - **1 May 1960:** bilingual Bombay split into **Gujarat** and **Maharashtra**. **Punjab Reorganisation Act 1966** (after the **Shah Commission**): **Haryana** from 1 Nov 1966; hill areas to **Himachal Pradesh**.
[261:6:7] ~~ Sources: Laxmikanth 8th ed. Part 3 p.156 (7th Amendment); Part 2 p.56; States Reorganisation Act 1956 text, ss.15-16 (thc.nic.in); app notes 1:261 (sub 7, 8, 9)

=== NOTES 1:262 | Formation of Andhra Pradesh 1956 – Visalandhra, Gentlemen's Agreement
## SUB 0 | Chief Ministers and Politics of United Andhra Pradesh, 1956–2014

  [262:0:0.4] P.V. Narasimha Rao | 30 Sep 1971 – Jan 1973 | Land Reforms (Ceiling) Act 1973; Jai Andhra 1972 → President's Rule 18 Jan 1973

  [262:0:0.12] N. Janardhana Reddy | 17 Dec 1990 – Oct 1992 | CM during the 1991 economic crisis

  [262:0:0.14] Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy | 14 May 2004 – 2 Sep 2009 | First term May 2004 – May 2009
  [262:0:0.15] K. Rosaiah; N. Kiran Kumar Reddy | 3 Sep 2009; 25 Nov 2010 – 2014 | Kiran Kumar Reddy = last CM of united AP
[262:0:1] - **Order asked:** Sanjivayya → Brahmananda Reddy → P.V. Narasimha Rao → Anjaiah (G2 Mains 2025); Sanjivayya → Brahmananda Reddy → **Kotla (1982)** → NTR (1983) – Kotla's first term came before NTR's.
[262:0:2] - **Never CM:** **Surjit Singh Barnala** (Governor of AP, not CM); Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao (Speaker); Pingali Venkayya.
[262:0:3] - **Sanjivayya "never defeated in an election"** = the false statement (G2 2008); he was the second CM, an AP minister and AICC President.
[262:0:4] - **Congress ruled uninterruptedly 1956–1983**; **1983** = the big change – a **non-Congress party (TDP) came to power with a large majority**.
[262:0:5] - **YSR** died in a **helicopter crash** in the **Nallamala** forest on **2 September 2009**; **K. Rosaiah** succeeded.
[262:0:6] - **Dismissal of NTR (Aug 1984)** by Governor **Ram Lal** → Nadendla CM 16 Aug → NTR restored 16 Sep 1984 → Indira assassinated 31 Oct → polls 28 Dec 1984 → NTR sworn in 9 Mar 1985; the crisis fed the **52nd Amendment (1985)** anti-defection law – a classic case of the Governor's discretion misused.
[262:0:7] - **Residual AP:** **N. Chandrababu Naidu** first CM of bifurcated AP (2014–19); **Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy** 2019–24 (5 Deputy CMs); Naidu again from **12 June 2024**.
[262:0:8] - **2026:** Governor **S. Abdul Nazeer**, CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu**, sole Deputy CM **K. Pawan Kalyan**; Amaravati made the sole capital by the AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Bill, 2026 (not Hyderabad).

## SUB 1 | Formation of Andhra Pradesh, 1 November 1956 – First Holders
[262:1:0] - **Andhra Pradesh formed on 1 November 1956** under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, on a **linguistic basis** – the first state formed under the SR Act; **Andhra State (11 districts) + 9 Telugu districts of Hyderabad State**; Kannada areas → Mysore, Marathi → Bombay.
[262:1:1] - **Andhra State** (1 Oct 1953): capital **Kurnool**; first CM **Tanguturi Prakasam**, Deputy CM N. Sanjiva Reddy; Prakasam's ministry fell on **prohibition** (1954) → mid-term polls 1955 → **Bezawada Gopala Reddy** CM. Before it, the **Wanchoo Committee** (Dec 1952) identified the **financial and administrative problems** of forming Andhra State; the **Pataskar Award** fixed the Andhra–Madras border (**Tiruttani** to Tamil Nadu).
[262:1:2] - **Capital:** **Kurnool = capital of Andhra State until 1956** (the "capital before 1956" answer); **Hyderabad became the capital of AP in 1956** – reasons: the SRC's view and the Mahasabha demand. Exam keys often call Kurnool "the first capital of AP".
[262:1:3] - **Andhra Legislature met at Kurnool** and backed the merger **unanimously**; **inaugurated by Prime Minister Nehru on 1 Nov 1956**.
[262:1:4] - **Name:** draft Bill "**Andhra Telangana**"; Communists wanted "**Visalandhra**"; the **Joint Select Committee** changed it to "**Andhra Pradesh**" – so none of "Andhra Telangana / Telangana Andhra / Visalandhra".
[262:1:5] TABLE head: Office | First holder
  [262:1:5.0] Chief Minister | Neelam Sanjiva Reddy (1 Nov 1956) – not Burgula, Sanjivayya or Prakasam
  [262:1:5.1] Governor | C.M. (Chandulal Madhavlal) Trivedi – also Governor of Andhra State
  [262:1:5.2] Speaker (first / "founder" of the Assembly) | Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao
  [262:1:5.3] Deputy Speaker | Kalluri Subbarao
  [262:1:5.4] Leader of Opposition | Puchalapalli Sundarayya
  [262:1:5.5] Chairman, Legislative Council (1958) | Madapati Hanumantha Rao
  [262:1:5.6] First Deputy CM | K.V. Ranga Reddy (1959–62, under Sanjivayya) – not Prakasam, Sanjivayya or Sanjiva Reddy
[262:1:6] - First ministry: **Bezawada Gopala Reddy – Finance**, **K.V. Ranga Reddy – Home**, Kasu Brahmananda Reddy – Local Bodies, J.V. Narsing Rao – Irrigation and Electricity, D. Sanjivayya – Labour.
[262:1:7] - Congress strength: 40 (Hyderabad 1952) + 119 (Andhra 1955) = **159**; **1957** elections only in Telangana (**79** seats).
[262:1:8] - **Legislative Council:** set up **1958** with **90** members; **abolished 1985** (NTR); revived **2007** (YSR) – again **90** members under the 2007 law.
[262:1:9] - **High Court:** at Hyderabad from **5 Nov 1956**; separate AP High Court at **Amaravati functioning from 1 Jan 2019** (President's order of **26 Dec 2018**, so keys also give 2018).
[262:1:10] - **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** became the **first Governor of Kerala (1956)**, later Governor of **Uttar Pradesh**.
[262:1:11] - **Capital pair (2002):** Andhra Pradesh – Hyderabad (now Amaravati, after 2014).
[262:1:12] > AP = 1 Nov 1956, SR Act, linguistic; capital Hyderabad (Kurnool for Andhra State); CM Sanjiva Reddy, Governor Trivedi, Speaker Kaleswara Rao, Council Chairman Madapati, Deputy CM K.V. Ranga Reddy.

[262:1:14] - **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy** was elected leader of the Congress party unanimously on **15 March 1953** (exam key; date not verified).
## SUB 2 | Visalandhra Movement and the Visalandhra Mahasabha
[262:2:0] - **Visalandhra** ("**Greater Andhra**") = the movement for **one state for all Telugu people** – the Circars, the Ceded districts (Rayalaseema) and Telangana, then divided between Madras and the Nizam's Hyderabad (in **1950** southern and eastern Andhra were in Madras State, Telangana in Hyderabad State).
[262:2:1] - Roots: 1912 Unnava Lakshminarayana and Jonnavittula Gurunatham sketched a united Andhra; 1914 second Andhra Mahasabha – **Nyapati Subbarao** proposed one rule for all Telugu areas; **1936 Andhra Congress Swaraj Party manifesto**; 1937 the idea spread in the Circars; 1954 **Madapati Hanumantha Rao**: the idea was 50 years old.
[262:2:2] - **Started / championed by the Communist Party** – demanded integrated linguistic states from **1946**; **Puchalapalli Sundarayya** coined the word and wrote ***Visalandhralo Prajarajyam***; daily **Visalandhra** from **June 1952**; Sundarayya later first General Secretary of CPI(M) (1964).
[262:2:3] - The Communists **became a great force in Telangana politics** and propagated Visalandhra **even before Andhra State (1953)**; they **did not oppose** integrated linguistic states (the only incorrect statement, G2 2025).
[262:2:4] - Other Communist leaders: **Ravi Narayana Reddy, Baddam Ella Reddy, Arutla Ramachandra Reddy**; the Hyderabad State Communist Party was a branch of the Andhra party (HQ **Vijayawada**); its 1952 electoral front = **People's Democratic Front (PDF)**. The Congress was first cold because the idea came from the Communists.
[262:2:5] TABLE head: Event | Date | Place | Key facts
  [262:2:5.0] Visalandhra Mahasabha founded | 26 Nov 1949 | Vijayawada (not Hyderabad) | Founder and president Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao
  [262:2:5.1] APCC resolution | Jan 1950 | Madras | Madras temporary, Hyderabad permanent capital
  [262:2:5.2] First Mahasabha session | Feb 1950 | Warangal | President Hayagreevachari; Hyderabad as capital; Hyderabad State split into three linguistic parts
  [262:2:5.3] Hyderabad Congress | June 1953 | – | Split into Visalandhra, United Maharashtra, United Karnataka
  [262:2:5.4] APCC, Kurnool | 30 Sep 1953 | Kurnool | Visalandhra with Hyderabad capital
  [262:2:5.5] Socialists | 21–22 Mar 1954 | Kurnool | For Visalandhra
  [262:2:5.6] Second Mahasabha | 13–14 June 1954 | Hyderabad | President Sri Sri; Swami Ramananda Tirtha strongly supported Visalandhra
[262:2:6] - **Kaleswara Rao** raised Visalandhra at the **1951 Bangalore** Congress manifesto meeting; he had translated **Gandhi's** Vijayawada speech into Telugu.
[262:2:7] - **Chronology:** **Dhar Commission (1948) → Visalandhra Mahasabha (1949) → Swami Sitaram's fast (1951) → SRC (1953)**.
[262:2:8] TABLE head: Work / paper | Author / detail
  [262:2:8.0] *The Emergence of Andhra Pradesh* | K.V. Narayana Rao
  [262:2:8.1] Pamphlets and a book | Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao (a supporter, not an opponent); also Kodati Rajalingam, Hayagrivachari, Paga Pulla Reddy
  [262:2:8.2] "Enni Naalla Swapnamidi" / "Emaanandam ... Eenadu" | Dasarathi / Kaloji
  [262:2:8.3] Nilgiri magazine | Published from Nalgonda
  [262:2:8.4] Rayyat (Urdu daily) / Imroz | Mandumula Narsing Rao / Shoebullah Khan
[262:2:9] - Telangana people were divided – not all in favour, and the capital demanded was **Hyderabad**, not Secunderabad.
[262:2:10] > Founded Vijayawada Nov 1949 (Kaleswara Rao); 1st session Warangal 1950; 2nd Hyderabad 1954 (Ramananda Tirtha for); started by the Communists.
[262:2:11] ~~ Sources: NextGen Modern India L2 Part 12 (src/ap-history/nextgen-modern-l2-12.txt) p.1; NextGen AP History Part 23 (src/ap-history/ap-history-appsc-23.txt) p.17-20; NextGen Previous Papers p.12; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.10, 12; NextGen Rocket AP History p.20, 43; Carpe Diem AP History G2 PYQs, G2 Mains 2025 Q30, Q41; old app notes row 262
[262:2:12] - **Communist Visalandhra centres:** **Hyderabad, Vijayawada** (party HQ, daily *Visalandhra*) and **Nalgonda** (*Nilgiri*) – literature, press and outreach.
[262:2:13] - **Visalandhra across both regions:** **Devulapalli Ramanuja Rao, Paga Pulla Reddy** (writers) and **Makhdoom Mohiuddin** (Communist poet-leader) carried the idea in Telangana and Andhra.
## SUB 3 | Gentlemen's Agreement, 20 February 1956
[262:3:0] - **Signed 20 February 1956** at **Hyderabad House, New Delhi** by **8 leaders – 4 from Andhra, 4 from Telangana**; the basis for the formation (accession) of united AP – **the united state took birth only after this agreement** (G2 2019); a moral and political understanding on the **Sribagh Pact (1937)** model.
[262:3:1] TABLE head: Andhra | Post | Telangana | Post
  [262:3:1.0] Bezawada Gopala Reddy | CM, Andhra State | Burgula Ramakrishna Rao | CM, Hyderabad
  [262:3:1.1] Neelam Sanjiva Reddy | Deputy CM | K.V. Ranga Reddy | Deputy CM
  [262:3:1.2] Gouthu Latchanna | Minister | Marri Chenna Reddy | Minister
  [262:3:1.3] Alluri Satyanarayana Raju | APCC President | J.V. Narsing Rao | Hyderabad PCC President
[262:3:2] - **Not signatories:** **Tanguturi Prakasam**, **Komarraju Lakshmana Rao** (d. 1923), Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao.
[262:3:3] TABLE head: Subject | Safeguard
  [262:3:3.0] Finance | Common costs shared proportionately; Telangana's surplus spent only on Telangana; review after 5 years
  [262:3:3.1] Education | Telangana students – priority or at least one-third of technical seats
  [262:3:3.2] Services | Proportionate retrenchment; recruitment by population ratio
  [262:3:3.3] Domicile | 12 years' residence for recruitment in Telangana
  [262:3:3.4] Land; Urdu; Prohibition | Sale of agricultural land controlled by the Regional Council; Urdu kept 5 years; prohibition left to Telangana legislators
  [262:3:3.5] Cabinet | 60:40 (Andhra : Telangana); at least one Muslim minister from Telangana
  [262:3:3.6] Portfolios | At least two of Home, Finance, Revenue, Planning & Development, Commerce & Industry – not "Home and Finance reserved"
  [262:3:3.7] CM / Deputy CM | From different regions
  [262:3:3.8] Regional Council | Statutory Regional Council for Telangana's all-round development (20 members); reviewed after 10 years; disputes to the Centre
[262:3:4] - **Cabinet ratio = 60:40**, not 3:1 (one NextGen page prints 3:1; the other NextGen page and the G2 2025 key say 60:40).
[262:3:5] # Regional Committee and Later Law
[262:3:6] - **Telangana Regional Committee**: **Art 371(1)** (7th Amendment, 1956) + **AP Regional Committee Order, 1958**; members = Telangana MLAs and ministers, **the CM was not a member**; first Chairman **K. Achyuta Reddy** (MLA, **Kodangal**); **extended five years in 1968**; wound up after the **32nd Amendment (1973)**.
[262:3:7] - Violations (jobs, domicile, surplus funds) → **Jai Telangana agitation, 1969**. **Art 371D** (**32nd Amendment, 1973**, Six-Point Formula) → **Presidential Order 1975** on local cadres and direct recruitment → **APRA 2014, Sec 97** extended 371D to AP or Telangana.
[262:3:8] > 20 Feb 1956, Hyderabad House, 8 signatories, 60:40, 12-year domicile, Regional Council; Prakasam not a signatory.

## SUB 4 | Hyderabad State Background – Mahasabha, Congress, Burgula
[262:4:0] - **Chanda Railway Scheme agitation (1883)** = the **beginning of public (political) consciousness** in Hyderabad State.
[262:4:1] - **Andhra Jana Sangham** (1921) – its **first meeting, Hyderabad, 14 Feb 1922, presided by K.V. Ranga Reddy**; it grew into the **Nizam Andhra Mahasabha** – first session **Jogipet, 1930**, **Suravaram Pratapa Reddy**.
[262:4:2] - **Hyderabad State Congress** (1938) – led and founded by **Swami Ramananda Tirtha**, who also led the **"Join Indian Union" movement (7 Aug 1947)** against the Nizam's claim to independence; integration by **Operation Polo, 17 Sep 1948**.
[262:4:3] - **Mulki rules** from **1888**, tightened by the **1919 farman** (about 15 years' residence); **Mulki agitation 1952** under Burgula – **firing near City College, Hyderabad**; inquiry under **Justice Pingali Jaganmohan Reddy**.
[262:4:4] - Hyderabad = **Part B State, 1950 – 31 Oct 1956**; Speaker at the merger **Kashinatha Rao**.
[262:4:5] - **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao** = **first elected (1952) and last CM of Hyderabad State** – Chief Minister of **Hyderabad State**, not Andhra State or AP.
[262:4:6] > Chanda Railway 1883 = public consciousness; Jana Sangham 1922 – K.V. Ranga Reddy; Join Indian Union – Ramananda Tirtha; Burgula = first elected CM of Hyderabad.
[262:4:7] ~~ Sources: NextGen Previous Papers (src/ap-history/nextgen-previous-papers.txt) p.19, 24; NextGen AP History Part 7 p.7, 12; NextGen Rocket AP History p.23, 35; kpiasacademy.com/hyderabad-feudalism-andhra-jana-sangham (Jana Sangham 1922); old app notes row 262
## SUB 5 | SRC, Merger Debate and the Leaders' Stands
[262:5:0] - **SRC** (announced 22 Dec 1953; Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru, K.M. Panikkar – not Harishchandra Heda) **heard opinions in Hyderabad in June 1954**; report **30 September 1955**. On **8 July 1954** a Hyderabad PCC delegation asked it for a **self-sufficient Telangana of 9 districts with Bastar and parts of Chanda**.
[262:5:1] - SRC **acknowledged Telangana's special claims** (finance, education) – **para 386**: Telangana to stay a separate Hyderabad State, merging after the **1961** elections if **two-thirds** of its legislature agreed; Raichur, Gulbarga → Mysore, Marathwada detached.
[262:5:2] - SRC's case for Visalandhra: **unified control of Krishna–Godavari waters**, minerals and power, **Hyderabad as a ready capital**, lower administrative cost.
[262:5:3] - **Hyderabad Assembly**: **103 for, 29 against, 15 neutral**; **Andhra Assembly (1955)**: Bezawada Gopala Reddy's **unanimous** resolution.
[262:5:4] - **Burgula Ramakrishna Rao**, earlier for a separate Telangana, **changed his stand in 1955** and urged **immediate merger** with Andhra.
[262:5:5] - 1956: to settle differences the **Congress leadership called the leaders to Delhi** → Gentlemen's Agreement.
[262:5:6] TABLE head: Leader | Stand
  [262:5:6.0] K.V. Ranga Reddy | Backed Visalandhra, then – as Telangana Congress president – wanted Telangana to remain a separate state
  [262:5:6.1] Marri Chenna Reddy | Against throughout
  [262:5:6.2] Swami Ramananda Tirtha | For – a separate Telangana would be weak and democratic forces suppressed
  [262:5:6.3] Burgula, Mandumula Narsing Rao, Pandit Narendraji, Makhdoom Mohiuddin, Mehdi Nawaz Jung | For
  [262:5:6.4] Tanguturi Prakasam | For – "Visalandhra nirmanam is the mother's right of all Andhras"
  [262:5:6.5] Kaloji | Supported, later opposed
  [262:5:6.6] Hyderabad PSP (Mahadev Singh); Harishchandra Heda (Nov 1955) | For a separate Telangana
  [262:5:6.7] Nehru (Oct 1953) | Called it "Andhra imperialism"; Rajagopalachari (1949) wanted multilingual Hyderabad
[262:5:7] # Arguments For and Against
[262:5:8] TABLE head: For Visalandhra | Telangana apprehensions
  [262:5:8.0] Integrated Krishna–Godavari planning | Weakening of the Mulki rules
  [262:5:8.1] Andhra's agriculture + Telangana's minerals | Advanced coastal Andhra would dominate jobs and education
  [262:5:8.2] Communists: land reform, weaken feudalism | Telangana's revenue surplus spent elsewhere; higher per capita income and revenue made it viable alone
[262:5:9] - Not a pro-Visalandhra argument: permanent protection of separate Telangana political institutions.
[262:5:10] > SRC in Hyderabad 1954, report 30 Sep 1955; Burgula turned 1955; K.V. Ranga Reddy and Chenna Reddy for separate Telangana.

  Integrated planning of which rivers formed the river-waters argument for Visalandhra?
  Tungabhadra and Pennar | Godavari and Mahanadi | *Krishna and Godavari | Krishna and Kaveri
  x: Integrated Krishna–Godavari planning was the river-waters argument.
[n36e50d421f2] sub5
  Under paragraph 386 of the SRC report, by what majority did Telangana's legislature have to approve merger with Andhra after the 1961 elections?
  simple majority | *two-thirds majority | unanimous vote | three-fourths majority
  x: The SRC recommended a separate Telangana initially, with merger after the 1961 elections only on a two-thirds majority of the Telangana legislature.

  H.N. Kunzru | Fazl Ali | *Harishchandra Heda | K.M. Panikkar
  x: Fazl Ali, H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar were the members of the States Reorganisation Commission. Harishchandra Heda was associated with Telangana political resolutions, not with the Commission.

  1953 | 1954 | 1956 | *1955
  x: The resolution, giving Telangana priority and population-based shares, was passed in 1955.

  *29 | 15 | 103 | 47

[n58a7d55ddc5] sub5
  Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
  Nehru announced the SRC in the Lok Sabha – 29 December 1953 | States Reorganisation Commission constituted – 22 December 1953 | *Report of the States Reorganisation Commission – 1955 | Visalandhra Mahasabha founded – 1953
  x: The SRC report came in 1955. Nehru announced the Commission on 22 December 1953, it was constituted on 29 December 1953, and the Mahasabha was founded in 1949.
[ncdd798799b9] sub5
  Which of the following territorial changes was recommended in relation to Hyderabad State by the States Reorganisation Commission?
  Raichur and Gulbarga to Andhra, and Marathwada to Mysore | Marathwada to Andhra, and the Kannada areas to Telangana | *Raichur and Gulbarga to Mysore, and Marathwada to be detached | All Hyderabad territories to Maharashtra
  x: The Commission recommended that Raichur and Gulbarga go to Mysore and that Marathwada be detached from Hyderabad State.
